538668|2026-03.headline: Meghna Infracon FY26 revenue rose 15.84% to INR46.2 crore, but PAT fell 4.28% as carry-over securities profits lapsed.
538668|2026-03.overview: Management described the company as transitioning from Naysaa Securities to a Mumbai-focused redevelopment developer. FY26 revenue from operations was INR46.2 crore versus INR39.88 crore, and Q4 revenue was INR18.48 crore, up 52.47% YoY. FY26 PAT was INR5.59 crore, down about 4.28% YoY, which management attributed to the absence of carry-over profits from the earlier securities business. Management guided to a sharp increase in GDV and profitability over the coming years, with current GDV pipeline stated above INR2,100 crore.

financial_highlights.change: +15.84% YoY vs INR39.88 crore in FY25
+52.47% YoY vs INR12.12 crore in Q4 FY25
Increase of about INR6.92 crore YoY as stated
Down from 29%, per analyst question; not disputed by management
Up from INR46,822 per sq ft, per analyst question

segments.name: Residential redevelopment (Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Five ongoing projects including Riviera, Rivaan, Pranam (Versova), Manju Villa and Joshville (Santa Cruz); ongoing portfolio about 290,000 sq ft and INR280 crore GDV. Goregaon projects 70-80% sold.

segments.name: Commercial (Meghna One IT Park, Wagle Estate Thane)
segments.commentary: Wagle Estate commercial project, GDV INR300 crore, launch date blocked for 22 June 2026 subject to RERA. Meghna One is a Grade A gold-certified green building.

guidance_outlook: Launches May-Dec 2026: Wagle Estate commercial (INR300 crore GDV), Khar residential (INR60 crore), Bandra West residential (INR240 crore), Juhu/Vile Parle West residential (INR50 crore); next launches adding over INR600 crore GDV by September 2026.
Upcoming portfolio GDV stated above INR2,100 crore; management aims to at least double it over the next two years, without giving a number.
Riviera OC expected within a month; Rivaan targeted for completion by December 2026 versus RERA deadline March 2027.
Management expects PAT to improve this year as project profits begin to be booked.
Approvals for seven to eight further projects with signed sign-ups expected in Q2 or Q3 2026 after BMC-level slowdown.
Acquisitions outside the redevelopment model to stay below 20% of GDV.
capex_capacity: Rivaan: 20-storey building, 17th of 20 slabs under construction; finishing on lower floors has started.
Kandivali project (over INR500 crore GDV): land registration done; height approval pending from MoD; company open to debt on this project, otherwise self-funded or pre-sales funded.
Construction area of current and upcoming projects to launch by December 2026 to exceed 1 million sq ft, with a similar increase expected over the next two years.
Biophilic facade design cited as cutting execution time by about 10-15%.
demand_pricing: Pre-sales typically 20-30% of inventory at each launch; Joshville about 70% pre-sold with about 15% inventory left.
Andheri under pressure from multiple launches; registrations on over 30% of Andheri pipeline expected in coming quarter.
Bandra/Santa Cruz/Khar project more than 70% sold.
Prabhadevi-Dadar sea-facing apartments selling at INR1.2-1.4 lakh per sq ft; company says its feasibility cost is much lower, enabling discounted entry pricing.
Price volatility in steel and cement: company seeks fixed-price contracts; management expects little impact on premium launches.
Realisation improvement attributed to premium project mix and maturing projects.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the about 12% rise in realisation: pricing or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a shift to more premium projects and maturing projects from prior-year launches, which lifted collections.

qa_highlights.question: Unsold inventory across ongoing projects and FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Riviera has one unit left; Rivaan six unsold units with bookings pending registration; Pranam 30-35% conversion this quarter; Manju Villa three units; Joshville about 15% left.

qa_highlights.question: Which of the upcoming projects launch in FY27 and approval timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Wagle Estate launch 22 June 2026 pending RERA by end-June; Khar RERA delayed by pending approvals, bookings in Q2 2027; Bandra West launch Q2 2027 with bookings from Q3 2026; Juhu/Vile Parle slipping 15-20 days into Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Kandivali approvals and funding plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Land registration done; awaiting height approval from MoD. Self-funded so far; open to project-level debt, with pre-sales and accruals as main funding.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT and EBITDA margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Securities carry-over profits ended after the 2024 transition; project lifecycle delayed profit booking; higher delivery costs and acquisition costs compressed margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative despite profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Company aims to stay nearly debt-free; cash went into acquisitions of future projects that management expects to lift GDV and profit.

qa_highlights.question: Pace of project addition and GDV growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to at least double GDV over the next two to three years, citing INR2,100 crore pipeline; no specific number given on project additions.

risks_watch: Approval delays at BMC/MoD level: seven to eight projects waiting, Khar RERA pending, Juhu/Vile Parle slipping.
Negative operating cash flow and reliance on pre-sales for funding; Kandivali may need debt or JV partner.
Margin pressure: EBITDA margin fell from 29% to 22% in FY26; acquisition costs and project mix weigh on profitability.
Andheri supply pressure from multiple launches.
Steel and cement price volatility on contracts that are mostly fixed price.
Rivaan completion target of December 2026 versus RERA deadline of March 2027.
538668|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on pipeline and demand, but evasive on quantified targets (declined to give specific project-addition numbers or land holdings). Cautious on approval timelines, with several launch dates shifting.
key_quotes: So to be very honest, there is not a dip in demand. Demand actually is impacted of by supply more than anything else.
We are nearly debt-zero. We have always maintained that we want to remain debt-zero and that's why you will see a negative impact.
In the coming three years, and I will not give you a number, but you can expect us doubling the GDV overall.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: FY27, as project profits begin to be booked
rows.why: Management expects PAT to improve this year, and the company says realisation rose to INR52,571 per sq ft from INR46,822 on a premium mix, but EBITDA margin was 22% vs 29% and acquisition and delivery costs are weighing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 to Q4 FY27 (launches May-Dec 2026)
rows.why: Dated launch pipeline of Wagle Estate (INR300 crore GDV, 22 June 2026), Khar (INR60 crore), Bandra West (INR240 crore) and Juhu/VP West (INR50 crore) by Dec 2026, with over INR600 crore GDV by September 2026; construction area of current and upcoming projects to exceed 1 million sq ft, but RERA and approval slippage is already visible.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Collections rose 36.69% to INR24.92 crore and FY26 revenue rose 15.84% to INR46.2 crore, with Q4 revenue up 52.47% YoY to INR18.48 crore, and management targets project additions of three to five a year and GDV at least doubling over two to three years, though the doubling is unquantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Kandivali (over INR500 crore GDV) land registered but height approval from MoD pending and company open to project-level debt; no utilisation metric applies since this is a developer, and no firm capex plan beyond project launches was stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides only to PAT improvement this year and an unquantified doubling of GDV over two years; no revenue or margin numbers were raised, and approvals are slipping.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Launch dates are already slipping (Juhu/VP West 15-20 days into Q2, Khar RERA delayed to Q2 FY27 bookings), seven to eight projects await BMC approvals, and EBITDA margin fell from 29% to 22% in FY26.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Wagle Estate commercial (INR300 crore GDV, launch blocked 22 June 2026 subject to RERA) plus Khar, Bandra West and Juhu/VP West residential launches, adding over INR600 crore GDV by September 2026.

rows.label: Pre-sales and sell-through on launches
rows.why: Joshville about 70% pre-sold with 15% inventory left, Bandra/Santa Cruz/Khar projects more than 70% sold, Rivaan six unsold units with bookings pending registration, and registrations expected on over 30% of Andheri pipeline in the coming quarter.

rows.label: Negative operating cash flow and debt funding
rows.why: Operating cash flow was negative despite profit as cash went into acquisitions; management aims to stay nearly debt-free but is open to project-level debt for Kandivali (over INR500 crore GDV).

rows.label: Approvals and RERA timing (Wagle, Khar, Rivaan)
rows.why: Wagle Estate launch depends on RERA by end-June 2026, Khar bookings slipped to Q2 2027 on pending approvals, and Rivaan targets completion by December 2026 against a March 2027 RERA deadline, leaving a three-month buffer.

tone.note: Management was confident on the pipeline (INR2,100 crore+ GDV, premium realisation up to INR52,571 per sq ft) but cautious on approval timelines, with several launch dates shifting; analysts pushed on the PAT decline, EBITDA margin fall from 29% to 22%, and the lack of quantified GDV targets.

538685|2026-06.headline: Shemaroo Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6% to about INR 132 crore, but EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR 2 crore from INR 56 crore.
538685|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was about INR 132 crore, down 6% YoY, with digital down about 17% to INR 56 crore and traditional up 5% to INR 76 crore. EBITDA loss narrowed sharply to about INR 2 crore versus INR 56 crore a year earlier, after about INR 20 crore of new-initiative spend; excluding that, existing operations EBITDA was about INR 18 crore. Net loss reduced to about INR 8 crore. Management said this is the first quarter after the inventory charge-off exercise, now in a normal charge-off cycle, and guided to double-digit blended growth, EBITDA-positive for the year, and bottom-line positive next year.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of approx. INR 56 crore (call analyst cited 55.5 crore) in Q1 FY26
materially reduced YoY; no prior figure stated

segments.name: Digital media
segments.commentary: Revenue approx. INR 56 crore, down 17% YoY, as select B2B syndication deals were deferred on geopolitical uncertainty; consumer business grew on fresh content and ad monetisation. Management targets double-digit digital growth.

segments.name: Traditional media
segments.commentary: Revenue approx. INR 76 crore, up 5% YoY, helped by closure of B2B licensing deals that offset subdued ad environment. Management expects roughly flat traditional revenue for FY27, with near-term ad outlook subdued due to BARC ratings blackout.

segments.name: ShemarooMe (OTT, Gujarati)
segments.commentary: Acquired OHO Gujarati catalogue in April 2026 (over 22 Gujarati originals); released 10 new titles in the quarter. Company does not disclose subscriber, ARPU or revenue figures; management said it is about two years from OTT profitability.

segments.name: YouTube
segments.commentary: Approx. 9 billion views across channels in the quarter; Shemaroo Filmi Gaane passed 74.7 million subscribers and Shemaroo Entertainment 61.9 million. Management said views are seasonal but viewership share remains strong.

guidance_outlook: Blended revenue growth aim of healthy double digits over the next 2-3 years; digital targeted at double-digit growth, outpacing recent low-double-digit industry digital growth by a couple of percentage points.
Traditional media revenue expected flattish for FY27, not declining.
Aim for EBITDA-positive for full FY27 (conservative view); management expects bottom-line positive next year (FY28).
Debt reduction plan for FY27, but no quantified target given; quarterly fluctuations possible given geopolitical and BARC blackout impacts.
Aspiration of around 20% EBITDA margin in 2-3 years, not a committed target; management said it is not sure it will be achieved.
New-initiative spend to be cut by more than 50% in FY27 versus FY26; management said the company is on track.
capex_capacity: Content strategy shifted: new content creation scaled down in traditional, while new content acquisition is being scaled up in digital.
Traditional channel rationalisation possible; company now runs two FAST channels after earlier shrinking the number.
OTT (ShemarooMe) needs ongoing content and customer-acquisition spend (ATL, BTL and performance marketing); management said little upfront capex is needed.
Inventory of INR 348 crore at Q1 end; management said no remaining write-down risk and the company is now in a normal charge-off cycle.
demand_pricing: Digital decline attributed to deferred B2B syndication deals (geopolitical uncertainty) and lumpy B2B revenue; consumer digital grew on fresh content and better ad monetisation.
Traditional ad market subdued for a long period; BARC ratings blackout in recent month has hit traditional and syndication revenue.
Acquired content is priced competitively against other bidders, so new-content margins are lower than on legacy content already amortised or charged off.
YouTube Shorts monetisation has not moved meaningfully; company is focusing on connected-TV long-form content, and is only experimenting with micro-dramas.
FAST channel ecosystem globally has been shrinking for roughly 12-18 months; company is tracking it and scaling only if monetisation improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA excluding the new-initiative investment, and what revenue is needed for positive EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding about INR 20 crore of new-initiative spend, EBITDA would have been about INR 18 crore. Management said margin depends on both revenue growth and cost cuts, and on revenue mix, so it would not give a revenue threshold.

qa_highlights.question: Is the content library under-monetised, and what growth is expected over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no under-utilisation, citing 9 billion views in the quarter. Traditional monetisation is declining while digital is growing. The aim is healthy double-digit blended growth, outdoing digital industry growth by a couple of points.

qa_highlights.question: Debt reduction plan and FY27 profitability and revenue mix?
qa_highlights.answer: A debt reduction plan exists for FY27 but no figure was given. EBITDA-positive for the year is the conservative aim, with bottom-line positive next year. Digital is seen at double-digit growth and traditional roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow digital faster, around 20%, given 9-10% CAGR over FY24-FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry underlying growth was low, and it would not burn cash to grow faster, since that would strain cash flow and the balance sheet. It cited its leadership in Gujarati entertainment.

qa_highlights.question: Which digital segments carry the highest margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin depends on content age, not platform. Legacy content can yield 80-90% margins, newly acquired content can be near zero or negative, and production work can earn 10-20%. YouTube is not inherently high-margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin, and is 20% EBITDA the aim on a reported basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was not satisfied with current margins and aspires to upwards of 20% EBITDA in 2-3 years. It declined to say whether this is on a reported basis net of all investments, and said the structural shift in the media industry is a factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and inventory at quarter end, and is further write-down likely?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was INR 311 crore and inventory INR 348 crore at quarter end. Management said the company is in a normal charge-off cycle with no further rationalisation planned.

qa_highlights.question: How long until ShemarooMe reaches break-even, and will it disclose subscriber or revenue data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is about two years from OTT break-even. It does not disclose DAU, MAU, subscriber, ARPU or platform revenue, and said it has no current plan to start.

risks_watch: Digital revenue fell 17% YoY on deferred B2B syndication deals; lumpy B2B timing could keep quarterly digital revenue volatile.
Traditional ad market remains weak and BARC ratings blackout is hurting traditional and syndication revenue.
Debt of INR 311 crore against an EBITDA-positive-for-year aim; quarterly debt movements may vary.
Limited disclosure: no OTT subscriber, ARPU or platform revenue data, and no quantified debt target; analysts asked for more granularity.
YouTube Shorts and micro-drama monetisation still unproven; a possible YouTube monetisation policy update was not confirmed.
538685|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the operating trajectory and cost discipline, but evasive on specifics: it declined to give debt targets, OTT data, profitability timing, or a revenue threshold for breakeven. It acknowledged margins are below its own aspiration.
key_quotes: Every quarter, I think we should be seeing an improvement on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
Are we satisfied with it? Definitely not.
I think if I see a 2 -3 year perspective, I think definitely upwards of 20% EBITDA is something that we should aim for.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Reported EBITDA improved from a loss of about INR 56 crore to about INR -2 crore, and ex the INR 20 crore new-initiative spend it was about INR 18 crore; new-initiative spend is to be cut by more than 50% in FY27, and management guides to EBITDA-positive for FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity is discussed; content creation is being scaled down in traditional, and FAST channels were shrunk to two, so no new capacity is planned in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets digital double-digit growth and healthy double-digit blended growth over 2-3 years, though digital fell 17% YoY to about INR 56 crore in Q1 and traditional is guided flattish for FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says little upfront capex is needed for OTT and the company is in a normal charge-off cycle; capex was not discussed beyond content spend.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is conservative on EBITDA-positive (described as a conservative aim), and the Q1 revenue fell 6% YoY, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Digital revenue fell 17% YoY to about INR 56 crore on lumpy B2B syndication deals, the traditional ad market is weak with a BARC ratings blackout, and quarterly fluctuations were flagged.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ten new ShemarooMe titles were released in Q1 and the OHO Gujarati catalogue (over 22 originals) was acquired in April 2026, so ongoing content launches are firmly under way, though no new brand or platform launch was named.

rows.label: New-initiative spend cut by over 50% in FY27
rows.why: New-initiative spend was about INR 20 crore in Q1 and management says it is on track to cut it by more than 50% versus FY26, which is the main driver of the EBITDA turn.

rows.label: Debt reduction plan for FY27
rows.why: Management confirmed a debt reduction plan for this year, but gave no amount, against total debt of INR 311 crore at quarter end.

rows.label: Inventory charge-off cycle normalised
rows.why: Management says no remaining write-down risk and a normal charge-off cycle now applies against INR 348 crore of inventory, which should stop the large write-downs that drove last year's losses.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost discipline, the EBITDA turn and content library strength, but evasive on debt targets, OTT subscriber data, profitability timing and a breakeven revenue threshold, and admitted margins are below its aspiration; analysts pressed on granularity and the path to profitab

538715|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, EBITDA up 45.6% to INR54.59 crores at a 20.6% margin, with the order book at a record INR174 crores.
538715|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, below management's earlier 20-25% target, because supplies on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and Delhi NCR were deferred by buyers. Profitability improved sharply: EBITDA margin expanded 460 bps to 20.6%, PAT rose 67.2% to INR30.14 crores, and Q4 EBITDA margin crossed 21%. The company deployed about INR27 crores of capex in FY26 under a Board-approved INR100 crores programme spanning FY26-FY28, and entered aluminium windows and facade with INR56 crores of orders. Working capital rose as management paid suppliers early and stocked PVC resin and polymers ahead of West Asia-related price increases.

financial_highlights.change: Management says it will not reach 0.75
Record high; vs INR120-140 crores last year

segments.name: PVC/UPVC polymer products
segments.commentary: Management said about 84% of FY26 revenue (about INR220 crores) came from PVC and UPVC, of which about INR60 crores was UPVC windows and the rest PVC profiles. EBITDA margin in this segment was higher than modular; PBT margin was about 16.6%.

segments.name: Modular furniture (Dynasty)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR43 crores (about 16% of sales), with PBT margin around 9%, which management said was up about 80% YoY. Four new builder brands were added, including Godrej, M3M and Smart Homes, and exports to Europe are growing.

segments.name: Plastic profile core segment
segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 13% and segment profitability rose 63%, per management. PVC profile capacity rose by 3,600 MT to 27,600 MT per annum, with utilisation around 66% in FY26.

segments.name: Aluminium windows and facade (Bangalore/Jaipur)
segments.commentary: New vertical under Mr. Varghese with INR56 crores of orders and revenue starting in Q4 FY26. Management guides INR40-50 crores of FY27 revenue; it targets EBITDA margins of about 20%.

segments.name: WPC doors and WPC wall/ceiling panels
segments.commentary: WPC door line (about INR10 crores capex) has finished trials and is due for commercial launch in Q2 FY27. Management expects about INR15 crores of FY27 revenue; WPC wall and ceiling profile lines are planned for Q3-Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Long-term target of about 30% revenue CAGR while sustaining EBITDA and PAT margins; management says 20%+ EBITDA margin is sustainable.
FY27 PVC profile extrusion volume growth of at least 20%; modular furniture growth of 20-25% expected.
FY27 new-capex revenue addition of INR55-60 crores, with aluminium facade INR40-50 crores and WPC doors about INR15 crores.
INR100 crores capex over FY26-FY28: about INR27 crores in FY26, INR35-40 crores in FY27 and INR20-30 crores in FY28.
Existing extrusion capacity can deliver more than INR450 crores of profile revenue at 85% utilisation; management did not give a year for reaching it.
Working capital expected to improve materially in FY27 as inventory is consumed and supplier payment cycles normalise.
capex_capacity: PVC profile extrusion capacity raised by 3,600 MT from 24,000 MT to 27,600 MT per annum in FY26; utilisation about 66%, with 80% cited as the practical benchmark.
WPC door line: machines commissioned and trials underway; commercial launch expected from Q2 FY27. WPC door capacity not yet finalised.
WPC wall and ceiling profile extrusion planned for Q3-Q4 FY27.
Aluminium windows and facade: Bangalore unit implemented; a new Jaipur factory site is under construction with capex planned in FY27. Custom fabrication, so no defined capacity.
Management expects ROE and ROCE of about 25-26% to be sustained on the new capex; it also said the new capex would earn similar returns across segments.
demand_pricing: Order book INR174 crores: UPVC windows and doors about INR84 crores, modular furniture about INR34 crores, aluminium windows and facade about INR56 crores; 100% expected to execute in 18-24 months.
Price hikes: three price revisions since the West Asia conflict began, up to 30 April. Management estimated 15-18% raw material cost inflation across its product lines.
Roughly 30% of revenue is fixed-price; B2B PVC profile distribution (over 60% of revenue) carries price revision clauses. Aluminium projects carry NALCO-linked base-price pass-through clauses.
Management said PVC resin fell from about INR115 in March to INR80-85 now; prices can move both ways.
Mobilisation advances of 10-20% of project value; net advances exceed INR7 crores versus about INR5 crores last year.
Management says WPC doors have no direct competition in India today; aluminium facade faces large international system brands and local fabricators.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the shortfall versus the 20-25% growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buyers deferred supply on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and one or two in Delhi NCR. Order book was healthy and the shortfall was described as timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is a 20%+ EBITDA margin sustainable amid raw-material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing product mix, upgraded offerings for upper-middle and high-end customers, and pre-buying of raw materials in February-March. It expects price revisions to offset the 15-18% input cost rise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did payables fall to almost zero and inventory and receivables rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it paid suppliers in full in the last two months of FY26 to secure supply during the Middle East disruption and bought PVC resin and polymers heavily in March. Receivables rose only in line with revenue, and it expects the cycle to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 volume growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to at least 20% volume growth in PVC profile extrusion, with new verticals adding on top. Price growth was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR100 crores capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly internal accruals (about INR50 crores of operating cash generation in FY26), with some borrowing. Debt-to-equity is currently 0.56 and is not expected to reach 0.75.

risks_watch: Revenue timing risk: deferred project deliveries by buyers caused the FY26 shortfall against the 20-25% target.
Raw material and aluminium price volatility tied to crude oil and LME aluminium; the aluminium contracts carry base-price clauses, but UPVC and modular contracts are largely fixed-price.
Working capital: inventory build, receivables growth and near-zero payables; management guided to normalisation in FY27.
Execution of the new WPC door launch in Q2 FY27 and the aluminium facade ramp-up, including the Jaipur factory build.
The 30% CAGR target rests on new verticals with no revenue history; management has not disclosed WPC capacity figures.
Margin sustainability: management says 20%+ EBITDA margin is durable, but competitive pricing and price-cut pressure are noted in the call.
538715|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on margins, capex and the 30% CAGR target, but defensive on the FY26 revenue miss and the working capital build. Several answers were vague on volumes, pricing and WPC capacity, and some figures were corrected during the call.
key_quotes: Q4 was our strongest quarter ever, with EBITDA margin crossing 21% and PAT growth of nearly 55% year-on-year.
Importantly, this is a matter of timing, not a loss of business, as our underlying demand remains robust.
Based on our current visibility, we are targeting approximately 30% CAGR revenue growth over the long term while maintaining sustainable EBITDA and PAT margins.
It's a cost-plus pricing, definitely it's a cost-plus pricing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 460 bps to 20.6% in FY26 with Q4 above 21%, management calls 20%+ sustainable, and price revisions are expected to offset a 15-18% input cost rise; competitive price-cut pressure is a counterweight.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: PVC profile capacity rose 3,600 MT to 27,600 MT in FY26 (about 15%), WPC door line starts commercial launch in Q2 FY27, WPC wall/ceiling lines are planned for Q3-Q4 FY27, and the Jaipur aluminium factory is under construction with FY27 capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides a minimum 20% growth in PVC profile extrusion volume, with PVC utilisation at only 66%, a record INR174 crore order book, and modular growth guided at 20-25%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: A Board-approved INR100 crore programme already covers FY26-FY28 (INR27 crore spent, INR35-40 crore in FY27), so new announcements depend on the WPC and Jaipur ramp; utilisation is only 66%, well below the 80% benchmark, which argues against an immediate new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order book is a record INR174 crore versus INR120-140 crore last year, and FY27 new-capex revenue is guided at INR55-60 crore, but FY26 revenue grew only 12.5% against a 20-25% target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 revenue missed the 20-25% target at 12.5% because buyers deferred UPVC projects in Maharashtra and Delhi NCR; the 30% CAGR is long-term with no year, and the WPC and aluminium ramps have no revenue history.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: WPC door line has finished trials and is due for commercial launch in Q2 FY27, with about INR15 crore of FY27 revenue expected; WPC wall and ceiling profiles follow in Q3-Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Record INR174 crore order book
rows.why: Order book is INR174 crore versus INR120-140 crore last year, with UPVC about INR84 crore, modular about INR34 crore and aluminium about INR56 crore, all expected to execute in 18-24 months.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation in FY27
rows.why: Payables fell to near zero after full supplier payments in the last two months of FY26, and inventory was built ahead of West Asia price rises; management expects the cycle to normalise in FY27, while net mobilisation advances rose to over INR7 crore from about INR5 crore.

rows.label: Raw material price revisions
rows.why: Three price revisions since the West Asia conflict, with 15-18% input inflation estimated; B2B PVC distribution (over 60% of revenue) has price revision clauses, but about 30% of revenue is fixed-price and PVC resin has fallen from about INR115 to INR80-85.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins above 20%, the INR100 crore capex and the 30% CAGR, but defensive on the FY26 revenue miss, the working capital build and vague WPC capacity figures; analysts pushed on volumes, pricing and the revenue shortfall.

538730|2026-03.headline: PDS FY26 revenue rose 4% to ₹13,110 crores, Q4 PAT nearly doubled QoQ to ₹72 crores, and the order book is up ~11% to ₹5,074 crores.

Q4 PAT rose about 95% QoQ to ₹72 crores on better operating leverage, cost control and lower finance costs. Net debt fell to about ₹105 crores from ₹374 crores despite the Knit Gallery acquisition. Management guided to mid-single-digit revenue growth and ~10% profit growth for FY27, with gross margin up 40-50 bps a year and opex growth below top-line growth; analysts pressed on the gap between order-book growth and the guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~16-17 day working capital sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Poeticgem and Simple Approach margins erode?

qa_highlights.question: Why does the order book growth (11%) not translate into higher revenue growth (5-6%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited customer caution on inventory and shipment pushbacks; UK and Europe order book is only ~3-4%, Asia ~8-9%, Americas ~30%.

qa_highlights.question: How does PDS keep winning share with retailers like Walmart?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth said 70-80% of retailer sourcing goes through third-party vendors and that PDS offers four services: manufacturing, strategic vendor (design-led sourcing), sourcing-as-a-service, and brands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the Ted Baker (New Lobster) business?

538730|2026-06.headline: PDS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% to ₹3,444 crore, EBITDA up 90% to ₹96 crore, and net debt fell 73% to ₹29 crore.
538730|2026-06.overview: PDS reported Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹3,444 crore (+15% YoY), with gross margin up 63 bps to 20% and EBITDA of ₹96 crore (margin 2.8%, +111 bps). PAT rose 43% YoY to ₹29 crore, though other income fell to ₹9 crore from ₹40 crore that included a ₹22 crore FX gain last year. Order book grew 23% YoY to ₹6,095 crore, and management announced new mandates with annual potential of about US$330 million. Net working capital fell to 1 day and net debt to ₹29 crore, with management stating a commitment to low single-digit working capital days.

vs ₹40 crore in Q1 FY26 (which included ~₹22 crore FX gain)

Depreciation increase reflects Knit Gallery acquisition and capitalisation of UK office property.
Ongoing SAP upgrade to S/4HANA and AI/digital investment across sourcing, pricing, supply management and operations.

US accounts reopened or added: Coles, Walmart, Fashion Nova, T.J. Maxx, PBS, American Eagle; management says 70-80% of key US accounts are now opened.
Europe: growth from Mango (Spain), CCC (Poland); Gerry Weber's bankruptcy replaced by new German accounts.

New Lobster (brand management) revenue ~₹100 crore in Q1; other licensed brands ~₹350 crore annually (~₹90 crore per quarter) and profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Order book up 23% and Q4 up 11% versus earlier mid-single-digit guidance; should growth be much higher this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said the order book has shaped up well and management is positive, but asked analysts to focus on Q2 repeating the Q1 trend and to revisit guidance after mid-year.

qa_highlights.question: Are new-vertical investments on track for the ~₹80 crore annual scale-down, given Q1 at ₹37 crore, and how will US investment and PBT be factored in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects more profitability over coming quarters and said the full-year P&L impact of new initiatives would broadly be in line with prior expectations; no explicit ₹80 crore reconfirmation was given.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost stayed flat despite lower net debt; will it keep rising with factoring as revenue grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Sadik Sunasara said interest cost is not going up, with quarterly ups and downs possible. Sanjay Jain said USD interest cost is stagnant and directionally flat or lower, with early payment discounts (EPD) offsetting interest, and more EPD-vs-gross-margin disclosure from Q2. Average USD borrowing cost is about 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI a cost-saving lever only or also a revenue driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth said AI currently drives productivity, citing a China subsidiary with 60 staff whose turnover doubled to $120 million, with local software under $25,000 a year. Customer-facing AI design helped win the French retailer contract.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1-day working capital a cyclical mix effect or structural, and could it return to negative as in FY23?
qa_highlights.answer: Sadik Sunasara said the 1 day reflects a higher share of factorable receivables; structurally management guides to low single-digit days, with 0 to 1 days possible in some quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Americas (+48%) and Europe (+21%) growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth said 70-80% of key US accounts are now open and volumes are scaling, with Coles, Walmart, Fashion Nova, T.J. Maxx, PBS and American Eagle cited. In Europe, growth came from Mango (Spain) and CCC (Poland), with new German accounts replacing Gerry Weber.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the 555 target today given macro and currency factors?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said 555 remains a long-term goal; the Gerry Weber and Matalan (about US$140 million to US$70 million) setbacks cost 12-18 months of stabilisation. Management now focuses on sequential EBITDA margin and PAT improvement each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the outsourced opportunity and how does PDS grow wallet share once inside a retailer? Is there a risk retailers bypass PDS to deal with factories directly?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth cited Marks & Spencer exploring a 50/50 in-house vs third-party split, with a US$100 million opportunity that PDS could serve asset-light with 4-5 third-party factories in about 6 months versus US$50-60 million of capex. He said standalone factories have little value and PDS's factories are the next tier, not the top 5-10.

qa_highlights.question: How much Ted Baker loss is in Q1 and for FY27, and what is the resolution path?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said Q1 Ted Baker PBT loss was about US$2 million and FY27 losses should not exceed US$2-3 million. Discussions with Authentic Brands Group are ongoing after franchisee administration in the UK and US.

qa_highlights.question: What profit can sourcing-as-a-service and brand management generate over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said the ~₹1,700 crore GMV under execution produced ~₹42 crore revenue (~2.5% of GMV) and ~₹10 crore PBT (~25% of revenue), excluding newly signed contracts. Brand management is separate; ~₹350 crore a year of licensed brands earns about ₹90 crore a quarter profitably, while New Lobster is about ₹100 crore a quarter and being fixed.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 delivery: management asked that Q2 repeat Q1 trend; guidance to be revisited after mid-year.
Finance cost trajectory: flat-to-down in USD terms depends on EPD offsetting interest; watch the promised EPD vs gross margin disclosure from Q2.
Ted Baker and New Lobster: FY27 losses guided at up to US$2-3 million; resolution with Authentic Brands Group still pending.

Account concentration and client risk: Matalan halved from ~US$140 million to ~US$70 million, Gerry Weber bankruptcy; US$330 million annual mandates and the French retailer GMV (US$300-400 million option) still ramping over 12-24 months.
Sourcing concentration: more than 50% of sourcing from Bangladesh; diversification into India (Knit Gallery) and Egypt is at early stage.
Working capital at 1 day relies on factoring of receivables; sustainability of low single-digit days and of the factoring-led interest mix.
key_quotes: So my request and specific response to your question is that let's stay focused on one more healthy quarter and maybe post the mid of the year, we can revisit any of the guidance or anything.

But rather than talking of 555 and the time horizon. We believe in it, what is important is that every quarter now, there should be improvement in the EBITDA margin, which we have achieved in quarter 1 and the corresponding improvement in PAT.

538734|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR171 crore with EBITDA margin at 23.6%, but order inflow lagged and management pushed new order wins into Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening on the acquisition front and what is the funds plan?

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and recovery from government clients?

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payables and unbilled revenue rise?

qa_highlights.question: Status and outlook of VTS (US subsidiary)?

qa_highlights.question: Order book execution period and pipeline?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 inflow would match FY26 intake (about INR350 crore) and exceed it by Q2 or early Q3. Three L1 projects, one LOI under execution. Analyst noted the INR800-plus crore figure referenced was revenue, not order book.

qa_highlights.question: Why is unbilled revenue high and is the accounting aggressive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it follows Ind AS and billing depends on government milestone certification, with about 10 major and 50 small projects on different milestone schedules.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate and FY26 decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower FY26 tax came from an INR8-9 crore refund and reversal of excess FY25 provision. Steady-state tax rate guided at 25%.

Installed capacity rose from 6,500 MT to 11,000 MT through an internally funded brownfield expansion, now fully operational from Q1 FY27. Management guided to about 95% utilisation (10,200–10,400 MT) in FY27 and a 5,500 MT freeze-dried coffee (FDC) plant by Q2 FY28, with a larger capex and debt plan outlined.

segments.name: Spray / agglomerated coffee (bulk and packed)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 11,000 MT after expansion from 6,500 MT; packed-form share rose from about 35% to about 53% in FY26, and FY27 packed share expected to grow a further 5–10%. Packing capacity is 5,000 MT with one more line being added, targeting a 40:60 bulk-to-packed ratio.

segments.name: Freeze-dried coffee (FDC)
segments.commentary: 5,500 MT plant with capex of about INR550 crore, of which about INR150 crore is spent; commercial operations expected from July 2027 after a three-month trial, with about 70% utilisation and about 9 months of output in FY28. A phase 2 of another 5,500 MT is planned for FY29-30 at INR370–400 crore, with land and building already being planned for it.

segments.name: Sales mix by geography
segments.commentary: Africa about 31%, CIS and Russia about 22%, Southeast Asia about 22%, Americas and Europe about 18%, local sales about 5%. Top five to six of 19–20 customers contribute about 45–50% of business.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume: about 95% utilisation of 11,000 MT, implying production of about 10,200–10,400 MT; Q1 has annual maintenance of 15–20 days and about 70–75% of FY27 sales are projected to be covered; Q2 projected sales of 2,300–2,400 MT.
FY27 realisation expected slightly better than FY26 on product mix (consumer packs and agglomerated); management cited 2–3% improvement.
FY27 EBITDA margin shows slight improvement over FY26; management targets about 19% (current 18.5% plus about 0.5% from utilisation).
FY28 margin expected to improve further (about 20–21% with 8–9 months of FDC output); FY29 margin 22–24%.
FY27 operating cash flow expected positive overall, with Q1 seasonally negative and Q3–Q4 positive.

FY27 debt expected to rise by about INR30–40 crore over FY26 at about 8.3–8.4%. Peak debt for the FDC project of about INR400 crore (INR300 crore ECB at about 5–6% including hedging, plus INR100 crore working capital at about 8.3–8.4%).
capex_capacity: Brownfield expansion from 6,500 MT to 11,000 MT completed in FY26 using internal accruals; expanded capacity fully operational from Q1 FY27.

FDC plant of 5,500 MT: capex about INR550 crore, about INR150 crore spent, remaining about INR400 crore to be spent over roughly the next year; commissioning by March 2027, trial run for three months, commercial operations from July 2027, completion stated as Q2 FY28.
FDC phase 2 (5,500 MT) planned for FY29-30 at about INR370–400 crore; management said funding through internal accruals may be difficult and ECB may be required.
Packing capacity 5,000 MT, with one additional packing line being added.
demand_pricing: Management said geopolitical tensions have had no direct impact as the company does not focus on Middle East or Western Asia; focus is Central America, America, Europe, Africa, Southeast Asia and Russia.
Coffee prices described as stable and expected to continue at current levels; packaging input costs (metal tins, aluminium) rose slightly and were passed to customers, improving realisation slightly.
Realisation management said is driven by product mix, not coffee bean prices; company operates a cost-plus model.
Global instant coffee production (including freeze-dried) is about 1,000,000 MT, growing about 30,000 MT per year, per management.
Management said it has no plans to enter retail; focus is on e-commerce and local presence.
EBITDA per kg for Q4 was similar to Q3; Q4 volume was 1,924 MT versus 1,802 MT in Q3 (one answer cited 1,824 MT for Q4 before correcting to 1,924 MT).

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of the expanded plant and expected run-rate?

qa_highlights.question: FDC capex and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR550 crore, about INR150 crore spent; remaining about INR400 crore over roughly the next year. Commissioning by March 2027, commercial operations from July 2027 (not a six-month delay, per management).

qa_highlights.question: FY27 and FY28 revenue and margin guidance?

qa_highlights.question: Phase 2 capex and funding?

538920|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58.4% YoY to INR161 crore and PAT 46.1% to INR20.8 crore, with 1,856 MT sold against 2,402 MT produced.
538920|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR161 crore (+58.4% YoY), EBITDA INR31.6 crore (+75.2%) and PAT INR20.8 crore (+46.1%), with a 12.9% PAT margin. The 4,500 MT capacity added at end-FY26 ran at about 90-95% utilisation, taking installed capacity to 11,000 MT. Management said the NCLT approved the merger of two wholly owned subsidiaries effective 21 July 2026, and freeze-dried coffee (FDC) capacity of 5,500 MT is under construction for start in Q2 FY28. Q1 was a seasonal lean quarter, with production exceeding sales and inventory building ahead of Q2 deliveries.

538962|2026-03.headline: Minda Corp Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR 1,704 crore (+29% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 203 crore at 11.9% margin and PAT of INR 124 crore.
538962|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly and full-year revenue, EBITDA and PAT for Minda Corporation, with Q4 revenue up 29% YoY and FY26 revenue up 22.3% to INR 6,185 crore. Full-year PAT rose 40.3% to INR 358 crore, helped by higher associate income from Flash Electronics and lower interest costs. Management highlighted new JVs (Turntide, Toyodenso), the planned consolidation of Minda VAST from FY27, and a FY27 capex plan of INR 400-450 crore. Commodity inflation (copper, zinc, aluminium up 30-40% through the year) is largely passed through to customers, though management flagged some EBITDA-margin drag from the lag.

qa_highlights.question: What laminate growth is expected in FY27 and is the company outpacing the industry?

qa_highlights.question: Plywood realisation outlook as the business matures?

qa_highlights.question: Peak laminate utilisation and need for further expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation has reached 108-110% annualised in the past and could get there again depending on mix. With two million sheets of capacity due by year-end and about 20% headroom at 86%, no further expansion is needed for now, and the position is reviewed quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook and breakeven timing for plywood and chipboard?
qa_highlights.answer: Laminate margin is expected at about 16-17%. Plywood and chipboard are both expected to break even in FY27; chipboard Q4 loss narrowed to about INR2 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Reports of particle board plants converting to MDF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not aware of any such conversions. It believes the processes differ and that particle board demand will grow with the QCO for furniture.

qa_highlights.question: Demand impact of the war-driven price increases?

qa_highlights.question: Why was the laminate volume decline not reflected in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10-12% guidance is on revenue; adding back about INR30 crore of deferred exports brings volume close to the target, and it still stands by the range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR135 crore net (INR70 crore laminate, INR40 crore maintenance, INR10-20 crore past payments), with debt expected to fall about INR100 crore; FY28 repayments are above INR150 crore per schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Is chipboard capacity enough, and when is more needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is sufficient; management will move toward pre-laminate mix and will decide on new capacity once utilisation nears 80-90%.

qa_highlights.question: Plywood target of about INR20 per sq m EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR20 per sq m equals about 8-8.5% EBITDA, achievable only at 80-90% utilisation over time; current realisation is about INR270-275 per sq m.

risks_watch: Export timing: about INR27 crore of shipments slipped from Q1 into Q2; management said it could not predict whether container and vessel constraints would persist for the full quarter, and a full-quarter continuation would hit export sales.

Laminate guidance: FY27 laminate revenue growth of 10-12% is reiterated despite Q1 volume down 6% and Q1 revenue growth of about 7%; management gave no quarterly volume or margin guidance because of raw material uncertainty.

Raw material volatility: chemicals (about one-third of raw material cost, up to 35% of laminate and chipboard content) moved up, down and up again; management said the picture is hazy and gave no freight or raw material normalisation view.

Domestic project demand: domestic laminate volume fell about 7.5% YoY as real estate and project customers delayed dispatches; management expects demand to improve with more market clarity but gave no timing.

Plywood breakeven: EBITDA breakeven is targeted within FY27 but would be a single quarter, timing unspecified; PAT breakeven may slip to FY28. Plywood utilisation is about 39-40% against a FY27 expectation of around 50%.
key_quotes: That is the reason which we have told that around INR25 crores, INR30 crores of export moved on t this quarter.
So margin, but in the past, we have already stated that laminate can grow at around 15%, 16% of the margin.
Entire year will be difficult. It is for that quarter.
Overall, on a net basis, we have passed on 7% to 8% of the price hikes.

539046|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 13.5% to INR896 crore and PAT grew 164% to INR40.69 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 6.84% on the Middle East cost shock.
539046|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: consolidated revenue grew 13.5% YoY to above INR896 crore, EBITDA rose 49.21% to INR92.21 crore at a 10.29% margin, and PAT rose 164% to INR40.69 crore. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR228.74 crore (up 20.45% QoQ, 9% YoY), but EBITDA margin compressed to 6.84% (INR15.64 crore) as freight, energy and raw material costs spiked after the Middle East conflict. The alu-zinc line was commissioned in late December 2025 and is ramping up in phases. Management said new contracts since April 2026 pass through the full incremental cost, and that H1 FY27 margins should recover meaningfully.

qa_highlights.question: Total capex outlay till FY28 and how it is funded?
qa_highlights.answer: The second colour coating line is about INR65 crore and the solar plant INR30 crore, both commissioning in Q2 FY27. Funding is a mix of debt from PSU banks and equity from the last fund raise.

qa_highlights.question: Will demand keep pace with 2-3x capacity expansion, given export concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports rose from about 20-25% of revenue three to four years ago to about 70% now. Management expects export growth to slow from 100% but still grow in revenue and tonnage.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable EBITDA upside from alu-zinc: pricing power or cost efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number. It said alu-zinc is structurally more profitable on cost and price, and the premium depends on cost, yield and utilisation (internal) plus demand and competition (external).

qa_highlights.question: Who will pay for the new cold rolling complex, and what are the ROCE and IRR?
qa_highlights.answer: Cold rolling is targeted within FY28, with no date, financing or supplier selection yet. Management said projects target ROCE above 20%, but this is not yet modelled.

qa_highlights.question: Will the elevated raw material cost persist into Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs remain high. New contracts since April pass through the full incremental cost, so management expects margins to be drastically better than Q4 FY26. A cost decline would bring a lag of about one to two months.

qa_highlights.question: Leverage threshold and future fund raising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not breach 2x debt-equity and aims for 1x-1.5x. No fund raise is planned now; the cold rolling mill would be next, with fund raising undecided.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue estimate from alu-zinc plus the new colour line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated INR300-500 crore of incremental FY27 revenue over FY26 from the new colour line and higher alu-zinc utilisation. It did not confirm a total FY27 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Alu-zinc premium over galvanized?
qa_highlights.answer: Ballpark of INR3,000-5,000 per ton on price realisation, depending on specification, gauge and coating grammage.

539056|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR178 crores and EBITDA 24% to INR90 crores (50.7% margin), with footfalls up 22%.

539083|2026-03.headline: Inox Wind Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue flat YoY at INR1,306 crore; FY27 guidance of ~75% revenue growth and 20%+ EBITDA margin.
539083|2026-03.overview: Inox Wind reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR1,306 crore (flat YoY), EBITDA of INR333 crore, PBT of INR216 crore, PAT of INR106 crore and cash profit of INR268 crore, with FY26 revenue of about INR4,500 crore against an earlier INR5,000 crore target. Management attributed the shortfall to geopolitical disruption: delayed imported ECS components, shipping and commodity cost pressures, and a PSU contract with payment delays. The company is pivoting from turnkey EPC to equipment supply, with equipment supply now about 50% of the order book and a target of 75% to 80%. Inox Green (O&M) reported Q4 total income of INR120 crore (up 40% YoY) and EBITDA of INR57 crore, and it is guided to above INR600 crore EBITDA in FY27 after consolidating two pending acquisitions and a demerger.

financial_highlights.change: INR400 crore shortfall expected to be recovered in Q1-Q2 FY27

capex_capacity: Inox Green's two acquisitions cover about 6.5 GW of operational wind O&M assets; entity one order expected within a couple of weeks, entity two expected within 60-90 days.

Evacuation infrastructure demerger from Inox Green into Inox Renewable Solutions approved by NCLT Ahmedabad; about INR1,000 crore gross block and INR50-55 crore annual depreciation removed. Completion expected in 1-2 months.
Cranes moving in-house (half in-house, a couple more due this year); power transformer manufacturing started last year and ramping up.
Management plans to expand into power electronics (transformers, inverters, power electronics, ECS) with details to follow in coming months.
Group Inox Clean has about 2 GW installed, 6 GW solar module and 3 GW cell capacity; targets 10 GW each of IPP, cell and module over about 15 months.
demand_pricing: Order book 3.1 GW, diversified; recent wins include Aditya Birla, Gentari/Amplus, Jakson Green, First Energy and Leap Green. Multiple customer negotiations near closure.
Order mix is about 50:50 turnkey to equipment supply, targeted to move to 75% equipment supply (management also cited 75-80%).

Management says margins are guided at about 20% or higher on equipment supply; equipment supply is on LC terms, passing steel price changes through, reducing exposure to land/ROW cost and payment delays.
Revenue mix: about 10% O&M and 90% Inox Wind currently; O&M expected to rise to about 18-20% of consolidated revenue.
Management said it does not have FY27 order inflow targets and is 'sold out' for about 2.5 years on its stated ambitions.

qa_highlights.question: How will the two Inox Green acquisitions contribute to EBITDA and when will they be consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both acquisitions carry roughly 50% EBITDA margins, as they are former OEMs with substations and evacuation systems. Entity one's order is expected within a couple of weeks; entity two is 60-90 days away, and all revenues from 1 April 2026 are to be reflected in consolidated results.

qa_highlights.question: What was actual MW execution in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give megawatt execution, saying the company guides on revenue only, and reiterated this stated policy.

qa_highlights.question: Will equipment supply shift raise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins stay at about 20% or higher, with equipment supply carrying less risk and more upfront cash; O&M at about 50% margin would add a higher-margin bias.

qa_highlights.question: Other income of INR61 crore at Inox Green: how much is recurring and how much is treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR40 crore relates to the two acquisitions (debt-linked, net of deferred tax, roughly INR25-26 crore at PAT level), INR10 crore is value-added services and INR10 crore is treasury income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Inox Green revenue fall QoQ from about INR78 crore to INR69 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the quarterly variation to value-added services timing (about INR8-9 crore) and said the annualised run-rate is the right measure.

539118|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR859 crore, up about 6% YoY and 3% QoQ, helped by better realisation, new clients and return of previously lost accounts. Realisation per ton was about INR8,147, up roughly 3% YoY, and daily tonnage crossed 11,500 tons. EBITDA margin was about 21.4%, down about 190 bps YoY from an exceptional Q4 FY25 (23%+) but up about 48 bps QoQ. FY26 total income was about INR3,245 crore, profit INR237 crore (up about 29%), and EBITDA margin 20.8%. Management guided to FY27 tonnage growth of 6-7% and kept an EBITDA margin of around 20%+ despite fuel cost pressure, which it plans to pass on via selective rate hikes and fuel surcharges.

financial_highlights.change: down ~190 bps YoY; up ~48 bps QoQ

segments.name: Tonnage / volume
segments.commentary: Tonnage decline was 13% in Q1 FY26 and about 7% for full FY26; Q4 returned to about 3% YoY growth. April 2026 YoY volume growth was about 8% per management.

segments.name: Customer mix (Q4 YoY)
segments.commentary: New customers contributed about 17% of quantity, lost customers reduced volume by about 14%, and existing customers grew about 1%.

segments.name: Commodity mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Textiles and cloth about 17-18%, agri (equipment, fertiliser, pesticides) about 10-11%, others (industrial, pharma, books, auto) about 5-6% each. Management says petrochemical-linked goods such as plastics are seeing lower demand.

segments.name: Booking mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: TO PAY and PAID spot bookings about 80%, ACCOUNT customers about 15-16%, FTL about 6-7%.

segments.name: Door-to-door
segments.commentary: Share rose to about 38-40% of commodities from about 33-34% earlier; realisation is about INR1-1.5 per kg higher for door delivery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 tonnage growth guided at 6-7% for the full year, with at least about 2% sequential growth each quarter.
New branches expected to add about 2-3% to FY27 tonnage; about 100 net new branches planned in FY27 (100+ gross openings, fewer closures).
EBITDA margin to be maintained around 20%+ (near 21% in Q1 FY27 per management), with some basis-point impact from the withdrawal of bulk fuel purchase.
FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore: about INR100-150 crore for vehicles and INR200+ crore for land and buildings.
Depreciation not expected to rise materially because most new investment is in land (non-depreciable).
Fuel price pass-through via selective route rate hikes, chargeable-weight change (1 cubic feet from 8 kg to 9 kg on certain routes) and fuel surcharge in contracts.
capex_capacity: Fleet: about 6,000 owned vehicles per management; vehicle count fell from about 6,100+ to about 5,900 YoY, with about 500 additions planned in FY26 (100+ done, about 400 more by December 2026) and no scrappage planned.
Network: about 1,293 branches and 50 trans-shipment hubs across 24 states and 4 UTs as of March 2026; about 110 branches opened in FY26 with about 55-60 closed, net about 40-50.

Hubs in pipeline: 2-3 locations including Nagpur and Raipur.
demand_pricing: Q4 volume growth came from new customers and return of lost accounts after contract restructuring; management says lost customers are returning due to service levels.

Fuel: diesel prices rose about INR3 recently; management said it has passed through on selected routes but not across the network, and that a 2x increase in rates within a week means pricing will be reviewed over 1-2 months.
Fuel procurement cost per litre rose from INR84.52 to INR85.54 as direct refinery purchase fell from 41% to 36% of volume (bulk purchase withdrawn).
Competition: most of the industry is unorganised; VRL says it is at a premium to unorganised operators but comparable to organised players and express cargo on corporate accounts.
Demand headwind: petrochemical and crude-linked goods such as plastics are seeing weaker demand, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume growth outlook and what efforts drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 6-7% full-year tonnage growth and about 2% sequential growth per quarter, driven by completed rate rationalisation, marketing, new branches and new customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will fuel-driven price hikes hurt volumes, and how is fuel cost passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume pressure is from weak petrochemical-linked demand, not fuel prices. Hikes were applied on selected routes, with fuel surcharges in contracts; April 2026 YoY volume grew about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of lower bulk fuel purchase?
qa_highlights.answer: Some basis points of margin impact; management said it is flexible to hold EBITDA around 20% and the bulk purchase facility has already been lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lorry hire charges rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet fell from about 6,100 to 5,900 vehicles while tonnage grew, so outside hired vehicles were used to carry the extra volume, plus higher lorry hire rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new branch contribution and depreciation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches contributed about 1-1.5% of Q4 growth; FY27 branches expected to add 2-3%. Depreciation is not expected to rise much, as land is a large share of new investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the business mix and competitive positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix is about 80% spot (TO PAY/PAID), 15-16% account, 6-7% FTL; door-to-door about 38-40%. Rates are at a premium to unorganised players and comparable to organised players.

risks_watch: Fuel price volatility and geopolitical risk; the pass-through lag could compress margins in the near term, per management's own caveat.
Weak demand in petrochemical-linked commodities (plastics etc.) could offset recovery.
Reliance on hired vehicles (lorry hire cost rose) while owned fleet shrinks.
Achievement of 6-7% FY27 volume growth depends on net new branches (about 100) ramping up.
Management did not disclose kilometre-based metrics; lead distance is about 270-280 km and capacity 15-18 tons.

But definitely, on a full quarter basis, we are planning to maintain similar EBITDA numbers.

539118|2026-06.headline: VRL Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose to Rs 81 crore (9% margin) on freight realisation up 9% to Rs 8,546/tonne and volumes up 9%.
539118|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose about 18% YoY to Rs 885 crore and EBITDA rose 22% to Rs 193 crore, with margin up 71 bps to 21.8%, despite a sharp fuel cost spike (procurement cost Rs 83 to Rs 94/litre). Management passed through the cost increase via rate hikes of roughly 5% in the quarter, and volumes grew about 9% YoY to 10.19 lakh tonnes. Net debt fell to Rs 391 crore from Rs 440 crore, and the board approved a Rs 280 crore buyback at Rs 320/share, subject to shareholder approval. Full-year guidance is raised to about 8% volume growth.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 5% was taken in Q1 across fuel-driven hikes, and it is sustainable; if fuel falls, rates would be cut 2-3%. Freight realisation of Rs 8,546/tonne would hold absent fuel changes and may improve further, as mid-quarter hikes are not fully in the Q1 average.

qa_highlights.question: Is 9% volume growth the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year volume growth now expected at about 8%, up from 6-7% guidance, supported by branch expansion and recovery of lost customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and how does it fund the buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual FCF of Rs 480-500 crore funds capex of Rs 220-240 crore and the buyback; debt will stay at about the current level (about 0.3x debt-to-equity).

qa_highlights.question: Why buyback rather than debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Buyback replaces dividend, as about Rs 175 crore was paid as dividend last year; debt is already nominal at about 0.3x debt-equity.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of DFC and rail on the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Company is in talks with the Ministry of Railways on hub-to-hub rail use; collaboration is minimal today and management says it would not hurt the customer-facing business.

qa_highlights.question: Karnataka minimum wage impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Rule not yet in force (challenged in court); impact expected to be small as salaries are already above minimum wage, with only statutory contribution changes.

539141|2026-03.headline: UFO Moviez Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 43% YoY to ₹1,342 mn and FY26 net profit rose 161% to ₹249 mn, though Q4 EBITDA fell 13% QoQ.

For FY26, revenue grew 15% to ₹4,864 mn, EBITDA 36% to ₹803 mn and net profit 161% to ₹249 mn. Management attributed the strong March to Dhurandhar: The Revenge, while receivables and DSO rose sharply because much of that film's revenue was booked at year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Why have trade receivables risen so fast (₹162 cr vs ₹115 cr), and is DSO a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the rise to higher ad revenue and a large Dhurandhar booking at March end. DSO was 147 days vs 121 in FY25 and about 134 in FY19; provisioning is adequate. Management agreed to show DSO for periods above 120 days in future.

qa_highlights.question: Is UFO losing pricing power as ad-sharing with theatres rose to about 59.5% from 33%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied losing pricing power. It cited multiplex mix, rental-linked minimum guarantees and aggregated inventory where UFO did not invest. It expects the ratio to decline as revenues scale.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said February was almost blank and blockbusters like Dhurandhar and Border drew wide releases, so other films avoided the window. Full-year CDC and VPF revenue still rose, and management says the business has stabilised.

qa_highlights.answer: Footfall and ProCAT are used to market the network to advertisers. Activation and off-screen advertising work has started but is at an early, phased stage.

qa_highlights.question: What was free cash flow, and why does debt rise while cash improves?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO did not give an FCF figure. Net cash rose from ₹48.3 cr to ₹59 cr despite about ₹15 cr tied in working capital including TDS. Debt is raised for theatre equipment via LC-to-loan conversions, and the company keeps both cash and debt by policy.

539141|2026-06.headline: UFO Moviez Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to ₹1,118 mn (vs ₹1,090 mn YoY) and advertisement revenue grew 33% YoY, helped by Dhurandhar spillover.

539150|2026-03.headline: PNC Infratech FY26 standalone revenue fell to INR 4,633 crore; management guides ~30% growth to INR 6,000 crore in FY27 with ~12% EBITDA margin.
539150|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR 1,458 crore with 12.02% EBITDA margin and PAT of INR 100 crore, while FY26 standalone revenue of INR 4,633 crore was below earlier expectations due to delayed appointed dates on four projects worth over INR 4,400 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR 6,000 crore (~30% growth), FY28 about 25% higher, and EBITDA near 12% in FY27, citing bitumen and crude-driven cost pressure partly offset by new escalation mechanisms. The company has an unexecuted order book above INR 22,000 crore, and it is diversifying into solar, BESS, coal mining and water. Net surplus on a standalone basis was INR 327 crore, while consolidated net debt to equity was 0.76 times.

segments.name: Highways (HAM/EPC/BOT)

segments.commentary: About INR 300 crore received in FY26 from state payments; FY27 revenue target INR 750 crore. Andhra irrigation: INR 380 crore work done to 31 March, ~INR 700 crore remaining, FY27 target ~INR 200 crore.

segments.name: Coal mining (MDO/item-rate EPC)
segments.commentary: Order of ~INR 2,956 crore over five years; FY26 turnover ~INR 68 crore; FY27 target ~INR 400 crore and FY28 ~INR 600 crore. Capex of ~INR 350 crore, of which ~INR 250 crore spent in FY26.

segments.name: Solar and BESS
segments.commentary: Order of ~INR 2,000 crore in development; physical execution to start Q3 FY27 after PPA with NHPC. Revenue target INR 600 crore in FY27 and INR 1,400 crore in FY28; equity requirement ~INR 400 crore, ~INR 120 crore in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue guided at ~30% growth to ~INR 6,000 crore; FY28 ~25% growth to ~INR 7,500 crore.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guided at ~12%; FY28 margin to be shared later, expected ~12% if commodity prices normalise.
FY27 new order inflow target ~INR 15,000 crore (INR 3,957 crore highways secured so far, plus ~INR 2,000 crore solar); 60-70% targeted from highways.
FY27 capex target INR 150 crore; interest cost expected to fall INR 3-4 crore from current quarter.
Equity infusion for HAM projects: INR 542 crore remaining over two years, ~INR 350 crore in FY27; internal accruals expected to cover it.
Revenue targets: Varanasi-Kolkata packages INR 1,600-1,800 crore; Jalna-Nanded and Pune Ring Road INR 1,500-1,600 crore; Haryana Orbital Rail balance ~INR 360 crore to FY27/FY28.
capex_capacity: Coal mining capex ~INR 350 crore, ~INR 250 crore spent in FY26; FY27 company capex target INR 150 crore.
Solar: land identified, connectivity in-principle approval received, final approval expected in 1.5-2 months; physical execution from Q3 FY27 after PPA with NHPC.

Two new NHAI HAM projects in UP (bid cost INR 3,483 crore combined): appointed date expected in Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: NHAI awarded 3,124 km in FY26, over 30% below the 4,500 km target; management expects awarding to improve but timing uncertain.
EPC competition described as cutthroat; management sees less competition in larger HAM and BOT-Toll projects, citing reduced bidder numbers on two recent HAM wins of about INR 1,700 crore each.
Company submitted 15 EPC bids and one HAM bid worth ~INR 14,000 crore; price bids expected to open before end-May and in June.

MoRTH cost escalation mechanism from 1 April 2026 for EPC/HAM/PBMC projects with monthly price adjustment (earlier three months); management expects revised authority cost or extended compensation for new tenders.
Back-to-back pass-through: SPV inflation indices (WPI/CPI) and bitumen price compensation flow to EPC contractor per management.
Vertis Infrastructure Trust: entire payment for the 12-asset divestment received, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY27 and FY28 revenue and margins be viewed given the FY26 shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided ~30% growth to ~INR 6,000 crore in FY27 and ~25% in FY28 (~INR 7,500 crore), with ~12% EBITDA in FY27; some margin pressure expected in Q1-Q2 from bitumen and crude costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the INR 6,000 crore guidance between approved and pending projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance excludes new orders; based on awarded projects with appointed dates, except Western Bhopal (~INR 100 crore assumed) and only 30% of the INR 2,000 crore solar order (INR 600 crore) is included.

qa_highlights.question: Will diversification into new segments hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no cross-subsidy effect is expected; earlier target was 13-13.5% EBITDA, now guided ~12% across the mix, with water and irrigation earlier delivering similar margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on the Varanasi-Kolkata packages and Haryana Orbital Rail?
qa_highlights.answer: Varanasi-Kolkata: INR 336 crore revenue in FY26, INR 1,600-1,800 crore targeted in FY27, no obstructions. Haryana Orbital Rail: over INR 400 crore done (53%), balance ~INR 360 crore to be executed in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost outlook and what drove the Q4 jump to INR 30 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 rise was from working capital utilisation and term loan interest on machine financing; management expects a reduction of INR 3-4 crore from the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company bid for BOT-Toll projects and how will asset monetisation proceed?
qa_highlights.answer: No BOT-Toll bid submitted yet; evaluating NHAI BOT-Toll opportunities and direct bidding is planned. Monetisation of the five PCOD assets is under evaluation; no framework announced.

Consolidated net debt to equity of 0.76x and rising working-capital-linked interest cost.

539199|2026-03.headline: SG Finserve FY26 PAT rose 58% to INR 128 crore on a INR 3,936 crore loan book (up 75%), with management guiding AUM growth of 25-30% medium term and 35-40% for FY27.
539199|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 operating income of INR 334 crore (up 96% YoY), closing loan book of INR 3,936 crore (up 75%, stated as an all-time high) and PAT of INR 128 crore (up 58%). Q4 PAT was INR 42 crore, up 30% QoQ, and Q4 fee income was about INR 6.2 crore against about INR 1.5-1.9 crore in earlier periods. Management reiterated nil NPA as its guidance and said it is comfortable with leverage of about 1.9x, aiming for 3x over two to three years without fresh equity. Q&A covered NPA philosophy, TReDS entry, related-party exposure and the sharp rise in fee income, and several answers were framed as conservative guidance.

segments.name: Supply chain finance (dealer / anchor financing)
segments.commentary: More than three-fourths of the business per management. Construction is the largest sector at about 35% of AUM, followed by automotive; average ticket about INR 5 crore per borrower.

segments.name: Factoring
segments.commentary: Bilateral factoring commercialised in March 2026 with INR 175 crore outstanding at 31 March. TReDS participation expected to go live in Q1 FY27 through RXIL and M1xchange.

segments.name: Cross-sell (LAP, working capital, business loans)
segments.commentary: Opportunistic cross-sell within the anchor/dealer ecosystem at near-zero acquisition cost; management said it is not a core focus. Mobile is about 2% of AUM.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of 25-30% CAGR medium to long term; FY27 aspiration of 35-40% AUM growth.
Profit guidance of 30-35% CAGR, measured on full-year PAT of the previous financial year, not Q4 exit run rate.
Profitability range: ROA 4.5-5%, ROE 14-16%, cost to income 13-17%.
Leverage to rise from about 2x to 3x over two to three years, in phases; comfortable range 2x-3x.
Internal AUM target of INR 10,000 crore in three to four years without fresh equity, with bank lines of INR 3,000-3,500 crore.
NPA guidance remains nil; management said the aim is no losses, while acknowledging that lending involves losses.
capex_capacity: Operates from 30 hub locations pan-India, each covering about a 100 km radius; business is 100% domestic with no import-export financing.
Bank lines of more than INR 3,000 crore, with INR 3,000-3,500 crore estimated, not fully utilised.
Gross disbursements for FY26 crossed INR 25,000 crore; Q4 disbursements about INR 7,700 crore against a book of about INR 3,900 crore (average churn about 45 days).
New businesses (unspecified) are under groundwork, subject to regulatory approvals; timing of FY27 or FY28 uncertain.
demand_pricing: Management said fewer than 100 of the top 500 corporates are active in supply chain finance, and only 25-30% of anchors' sales are covered by organised programmes, so headroom is large.

Management estimated the wider supply chain market, including PSU banks, at upward of INR 1 lakh crore; five to six private banks and a few NBFCs each run AUM of INR 10,000-15,000 crore in dealer finance.
Fee income is being pursued as a strategy; fees on disbursements range from 10 paise to 50 paise, with some cases at 1%.
Management said no stress is visible in top sectors but is monitoring geopolitical and fuel/gas supply risks; steel import effects are yet to be assessed.

qa_highlights.question: How does the business model support nil NPAs, and is there a buffer in NPA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exposure is short-term (about 45-day churn), invoice-backed and end-use monitored, with anchors paid directly and early-warning tracking of dealer cycles. It said Ind AS ECL and RBI rules limit conservative provisioning, with about INR 18 crore provision already held; the guidance is nil NPA by design.

qa_highlights.question: What is the leverage target and how will growth be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Leverage is about 1.9x; management sees 3x as acceptable and aims to reach it in two to three years in phases. Bank lines of INR 3,000-3,500 crore are available, so growth to INR 10,000 crore AUM is possible in three to four years without fresh equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fee income is now a strategic focus and that Q3 fees were under-captured; it expects Q4-level fees (about INR 6 crore) to become the norm.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% growth guidance conservative, and is FY27 guidance different?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is deliberately conservative and aims for 35-40% AUM growth in FY27, with 25-30% as the medium-term average. Earlier conservatism was attributed to a management change.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the loan book goes to group companies?
qa_highlights.answer: Related-party exposure is less than INR 100 crore; channel financing to group companies is around 30% of the overall book.

qa_highlights.question: Did steel prices drive the AUM increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the steel price rise did not drive the 31 March AUM; growth came from volume and FY26 average AUM doubled to INR 2,640 crore.

risks_watch: Fee income reliance: Q4 fee income of about INR 6.2 crore is far above prior quarters; sustainability is unproven.
Geopolitical and fuel/gas supply disruption could stress steel, auto and construction borrowers (top sectors), though no stress was reported.
Earlier guidance inconsistency across quarters, which an investor raised; conservative framing may need to be tracked against actuals.
Leverage increase from 1.9x to 3x and the timing of TReDS go-live in Q1 FY27 and of new business approvals.
Concentration in the construction sector (about 35% of AUM).
