539199|2026-06.headline: SG Finserve posts record Q1 FY27 PBT of INR72 crore (+27% QoQ) and loan book of INR4,552 crore (+82% YoY) with nil NPAs.
539199|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly PBT of INR72 crore, up 27% QoQ, with the loan book rising 16% QoQ to INR4,552 crore. Net worth reached INR1,539 crore, leverage moved to 2.2x from 1.9x at March 2026, and CRAR stood at 32%. Annualised ROA was 5.1% and ROE 14%, with nil NPAs reported. Management reiterated FY27 PBT visibility of about INR300 crore (about 75% YoY), with AUM guidance of INR5,500 crore for FY27 and a 25-30% AUM CAGR over three to four years.

segments.name: Supply chain finance and working capital
segments.commentary: Management said about two-thirds of business financing sits in working capital, supply chain and factoring; about one-third of AUM is from the APL Apollo ecosystem, down from a higher share, and 52 anchor mandates are running (5 added in Q1).

segments.name: Factoring (TReDS and bilateral)
segments.commentary: Factoring outstanding was INR225 crore in June versus INR175 crore in March; commercialised in March-April 2026, with yields at par with channel finance for TReDS and at or slightly above for bilateral deals.

segments.name: Beyond supply chain (cross-sell LAP, opportunistic)
segments.commentary: Roughly one-third of business financing; management named digital lending and loan against property as products under consideration, with no retail or consumer lending.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PBT visibility of about INR300 crore (about 75% YoY); PAT about INR225 crore; FY27 closing equity about INR1,700 crore; FY27 AUM about INR5,500 crore (management called INR6,000 crore aspirational).
Targeted AUM CAGR of 25-30% over three to four years, with profitability CAGR of 30-35%; INR10,000 crore AUM now targeted for FY30 (earlier guidance was INR7,500 crore for FY30) and possibly FY29.
Quarter-on-quarter growth normalised to about 8-10% for PAT, with AUM growth of about 15-16% QoQ, after adjusting for INR337 crore equity received at end-March and early April.
Cost-to-income to be kept below 15%; opex maintained at about 1% of average book.
Leverage to move from 2x towards 3x over about two years, taking ROE from 14% towards 16% with ROA held at around 4.5-5%. No equity raise planned through the growth phase up to INR10,000 crore AUM.
Insurance broking subsidiary (SG Insurance Brokers) incorporated; IRDAI licence pending, commercialisation at least two to three quarters away, and not expected before Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: No capex or physical capacity discussed; the business is asset-light, with about 30 locations for sales coverage.
ESOP pool of 20 lakh approved by shareholders; about 10.32 lakh granted in April and about 50,000 granted in July to new joiners, leaving about 9 lakh unallocated with no timing decided.
GIFT City entity approval received from the board, subject to dual RBI and IFSCA approvals; long-term plan.
Board has approved AIF and ARC business; no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Average portfolio yield held at about 12.5% in Q3, Q4 and Q1, with factoring added without diluting or enhancing the overall yield.
Management said geopolitical uncertainty is hitting the MSME and trader business through lower incremental working capital needs, but has not yet translated into credit pressure.

Management said it does not compete with large banks and NBFCs, and fills the gap left when a dealer's bank working capital limit falls short of its requirement; for example, INR2 crore gap on a INR10 crore need.
Management estimated the addressable market as receivables of about INR25 lakh crore on the balance sheets of the top 1,000 corporates.
Management said the MoU-based anchor pipeline (52 anchors, INR7,700 crore MoU value) is a dummy limit and should not be read as book visibility.

qa_highlights.question: Will equity be raised this year, given net worth near INR1,510 crore and projected FY27 book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity raise is needed; net worth is INR1,539 crore at 30 June, and FY27 closing equity should be about INR1,700 crore, with leverage rising from 2x towards 3x over about two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 AUM guidance only 25-30% CAGR when growth is far higher currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called itself a conservative lender, citing the aim of nil NPAs, low credit cost and a balance sheet able to absorb shocks; 25-30% AUM CAGR is described as healthy and sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Is NPA-free status sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nil NPA is the stated aim, but acknowledged that losses can occur in lending; a larger net worth and profitability would be the buffer.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q1 run rate persist, given that H2 is usually stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR4,000 crore average book sustains the base, with incremental growth on top; QoQ PAT growth of 8-10% is targeted after normalising the equity infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cost-to-income only 7% against a 14% guide?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified the right metric is opex at about 1% of average book, and the company guides to cost-to-income below 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is SG Insurance Brokers and when will it start?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a wholly owned subsidiary for B2B fee-based cross-sell to the existing anchor and borrower ecosystem, not underwriting; subject to IRDAI approval and at least two to three quarters away.

risks_watch: Credit risk without NPAs: management concedes losses can occur, and nil NPA is a stated aim, not a guarantee.
Geopolitical stress on MSME and trader working-capital demand could slow new business growth, though credit costs are so far unaffected.
Q1 PBT was boosted by equity received in late March and April (INR337 crore), so QoQ growth should normalise to about 8-10%.
Guidance has been raised in substance (INR10,000 crore AUM by FY30 versus INR7,500 crore earlier), so next-quarter delivery against the INR5,500 crore FY27 AUM target should be tracked.
Insurance broking and factoring scale-up depend on regulatory approvals and team build-out; factoring is still small (about 5% of AUM).

539199|2026-09.headline: SG Finserve posted an all-time high quarterly PAT of INR59 crore in Q2 FY27, with loan book at ~INR5,700 crore and H1 PBT of INR150 crore.
539199|2026-09.overview: Management reported record Q2 FY27 PAT of INR59 crore and a loan book of about INR5,700 crore, up roughly 25% QoQ on period-end basis (average AUM up 17% QoQ). Asset-to-equity rose from 2.8x to 3.7x over the last year, and quarterly ROE reached about 15%. Management revised its mid-term debt-to-equity ceiling from 3x to 4x, which it said would take AUM to about INR11,000 crore, and it expects no equity raise this year. New initiatives during the quarter included factoring/TReDS, digital lending, loan against property (LAP), and a stake in an AI/digital subsidiary, plus a GIFT City subsidiary and an AIF pending SEBI approval.

segments.name: Supply chain finance (dealer / deep-tier)
segments.commentary: Supply chain is ~70% of AUM. Group ecosystem share of book has fallen to 25%; the company powers ~60 brands. Steel and building products ~35% of AUM and auto ~20%.

segments.name: Factoring / TReDS
segments.commentary: Factoring licence received in March 2026; now ~15% of book after starting in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Digital lending (BharatPe merchant LSP model)
segments.commentary: ~10,000 loans disbursed; book only INR121 crore at 30 Sep 2026. Management expects ~10% of AUM in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP) / business loans
segments.commentary: Just started in Delhi NCR with four disbursals and INR17 crore outstanding; tickets above INR25 lakh.

segments.name: Project finance
segments.commentary: 12 accounts disbursed recently, none commercially operational; management expects starts in 6-9 months.

guidance_outlook: Debt-to-equity mid-term ceiling revised from 3x to 4x; board approved incremental borrowing in the call's board meeting.
AUM growth guidance of 30-35% CAGR on a one-year-forward basis; profitability CAGR guidance of 35-40%.
Management targets INR10,000-11,000 crore AUM in 2-3 years, implying ~100% growth from current book; equity dilution or higher leverage mandate expected only after that.
Full-year PAT guidance of INR225 crore reiterated; management said it may do slightly better.
Expects around 7,000 crore AUM by year end on current run rate (per management comment); Q2/Q4 seasonality of 2-3% on the higher side.
Target of adding 2 anchor corporates per month for the next 12-18 months.
GIFT City finance subsidiary (~INR48 crore investment approved) expected operational in about a year, subject to RBI and IFSCA approvals.
Planning to keep ROA above 4.5% and cost-to-income below 15%; yield maintained at ~13% on AUM.
capex_capacity: Headcount ~100 (roughly doubled in one year); per-employee annualised PAT above INR2 crore; presence in 34 locations.
Digital lending built on LSP framework; in-house AI/digital stack being built via a 15% stake in a subsidiary rather than external SaaS.
New subsidiaries: AIF (Cat III equity AIF, SEBI approval awaited), AMC subsidiary, GIFT City finance company (~INR48 crore), shared services company (cost amount undecided), AI/technology subsidiary.
Project finance: 12 accounts, none yet operational.

demand_pricing: Wallet share across the ~60 anchor brands is under 5%; management targets doubling to 10%, plus 20-25 new brands in the next year.

Lending rates are benchmarked to the SGFL benchmark rate; management said any repo-linked cost increase would be passed on, though benchmark not yet raised.
Management positions the company as filling the INR10-20 'untied' portion of borrowers' funding need after banks/NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity this financial year, given borrowings near 3x net worth?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Debt-to-equity mandate raised to 4x, with incremental borrowing approved by the board; equity dilution or higher leverage considered 2-3 years out.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue grow ~18% QoQ while AUM grew 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Income accrues on daily outstanding; average AUM grew 17% QoQ, so period-end growth overstates income growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost as a percentage of income rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher leverage (asset-to-equity 2.8x to 3.7x); management said this lifts ROE.

qa_highlights.question: What is the collection efficiency and DPD profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly collection efficiency 99.5%; 60+ DPD is zero overall and 30+ DPD is zero in non-supply-chain book; 0.5% slips to 1+ DPD and is mostly collected within 30 DPD.

qa_highlights.question: How does the RBI draft on revolving credit affect the model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the product is term-based with no rollover or extension, so it is aligned; only documentation and reporting systems need tweaks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds and funding mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Single source is banks and NBFCs (19 lenders), plus opportunistic commercial paper; cost of borrowing about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 credit cost increase a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Provisioning is an ECL/IRAC regulatory requirement, not cash credit cost; ~INR25 crore accumulated on ~INR5,700 crore book, and nil NPA is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Why would borrowers choose SG over banks?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowers often get INR80-90 of a INR100 requirement from banks; SG funds the remaining untied portion, under a coexistence model across PSU banks, private banks, large NBFCs and mid-layer NBFCs.

risks_watch: Leverage rising toward the 4x D/E ceiling; equity dilution likely around INR10,000-11,000 crore AUM given the ~3x price-to-book; watch the CCD/OCD option.
Finance cost ratio rising (44.5% of interest income); repo hike and benchmark pass-through timing unclear.
Draft RBI norms on revolving credit could require documentation and system changes for supply-chain products (about two-thirds of AUM).
BharatPe digital-lending book: management acknowledged gross NPAs are possible, relying on FLDG and LSP cushions.
New businesses (AIF, GIFT City, LAP, project finance) carry execution and gestation risk; project finance accounts not yet operational.
Management said the Q2 front-loading of growth may normalise; the 30-35% growth guide must be tested in H2.
Opex discipline as headcount and locations expand; the cost-to-income target is below 15%.

539221|2026-03.headline: Sportking expects top line up 7-10% and margins to expand 15-20% QoQ over next three quarters on higher yarn prices and a long sales book.
539221|2026-03.overview: Management described a resilient Q4 FY26 with revenue broadly stable and profitability improved, driven by better yarn realisation and stronger cotton yarn demand. Demand was attributed to China's resurgence as a cotton yarn importer, Bangladesh recovery, and a stronger rupee-driven competitiveness shift for Indian spinning. Management said spreads are at roughly three-year highs and expects margins to expand over the next two to three quarters, with the 150,000-spindle greenfield project slated for commercial operations in Q3 FY27. Acquisitions of a majority stake in Marvel Dyers and Processors and the Sobhagia Sales manufacturing facilities were approved, with closure targeted within the calendar year.

financial_highlights.value: Broadly stable (no figure stated on call)

financial_highlights.change: Expected to reverse in Q1 if rupee does not depreciate further
Management estimate for current/coming financial year

segments.commentary: Demand robust across segments for last 2-3 months; yarn prices moved from about USD2.70-2.80/kg average last quarter to near USD3.30 now. Export book covers about 90 days, with the current quarter largely sold.

segments.name: Acquired entities (Marvel Dyers and Processors; Sobhagia Sales facilities)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue about INR200 crores (7-8% of turnover). Group companies expected to be flattish in FY26 and grow 15-20% in FY27 after reengineering, versus management's earlier 20-25% framing.

guidance_outlook: Top line expected to rise 7-10% over the next three quarters on higher yarn prices; no volume growth as plant runs at 95-96% optimum utilisation.

Quarter-on-quarter margin expansion targeted at least 15-20% over the next two to three quarters, supported by spreads and the long sales book; management said it would be disappointed not to deliver 15%+ margins in H1 but declined to give formal guidance.

Greenfield 150,000-spindle expansion (approx. INR1,000 crores) expected to start commercial operations in Q3 FY27, with a little contribution in Q3 and a more substantial contribution from Q4 and fully from FY28.
40 MW solar to commence by end-May 2026, saving INR14-15 crores annually.
Acquisitions expected to close within the current calendar year at the latest; bigger downstream plans to be shared after 6-9 months of integration.
EU and UK FTAs expected to be effective by end of FY27 (UK in 2-3 months, EU in about 6 months per management's read of government sources).
capex_capacity: Greenfield expansion of approximately INR1,000 crores adds about 150,000 spindles; land acquired, machinery advances released, construction on schedule, commercial operations targeted Q3 FY27 in Odisha.
Ramp-up: first output about 2 months after commissioning, then about 15-16% of capacity added each month; 97-98% utilisation expected about 6 months after commissioning.

40 MW solar plant to commence by end-May 2026 under Punjab policy, supplying about 7 crore units per year at about INR3.70/unit, saving about INR2/unit (INR14-15 crores annually). Management said no further ground-mounted solar planned in Odisha, only possible small rooftop solar.

Acquisition of majority stake in Marvel Dyers and Processors Pvt Ltd approved by Board; acquisition of manufacturing facilities of Sobhagia Sales Pvt Ltd on slump-sale basis and land and building on lease basis, subject to definitive agreements and approvals.
Current plant running at about 95-96% of optimum capacity.
demand_pricing: China's share of Indian cotton yarn exports rose from about 7-8% to roughly 25-30% per management; Sportking's China exports rose from about 2-3% to about 10-12% of its exports in the last quarter.
Bangladesh remains Sportking's largest export market; domestic demand has picked up since March after the US tariff removal.
Cotton yarn spread about USD1.00/kg (skein cost vs. yarn price) versus USD0.65-0.70 over the last couple of years; cotton spreads at about 3-year highs.
Cotton covered for 3-6 months; management did not disclose coverage levels, saying all good mills cover most of the season's cotton by end-March.

CCI bought 106 lakh bales of a projected 310 lakh bale crop (about 33-34%), which management says lifts market prices toward MSP at harvest; government import-duty relief on cotton awaited within a couple of months.
Export mix roughly 50% international, plus or minus 5%, which management expects to stay in this range with FTAs.

qa_highlights.question: How will new capacity ramp, and why are spreads rising and sustainable for 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads supported by a 90-day export book already largely sold for the current quarter and cotton covered for 3-6 months. New greenfield capacity is on timeline, with 97-98% utilisation about 6 months after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Is China a durable demand source given historical volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged volatility but said Chinese domestic demand has turned after 4-5 years of weakness and that China now needs to import cotton given peaking domestic production and high cotton duties.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to margins once new-crop cotton prices fall or rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current spreads are among the best of the last 3 years even at today's cotton prices; April-September is seasonally weak and October-March is seasonally stronger. No crystal ball on pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for H1 FY27 and quarter-on-quarter trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects QoQ margin expansion of at least 15-20% over the next 2-3 quarters, citing higher yarn prices (USD3.30 vs USD2.70-2.80) and the long sales book. It declined to give formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the acquisitions and synergies on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired entities are about 7-8% of turnover (about INR200 crores). Immediate margin impact is small; they serve as labs for downstream expansion. Closure expected this calendar year at the latest.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin and the forex hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Better spreads and robust demand drove margin; some small provisions held it back. The forex loss was a notional mark-to-market on unshipped and unreceived items at the all-time-high dollar on 31 March, expected to reverse if the rupee does not weaken further. Management said it books sales the same day and holds no open risk.

risks_watch: Chinese demand volatility; management acknowledged China has been a volatile market.
New-crop cotton prices and procurement cost in October onward could compress spreads; no guidance given on post-H1 margins.
Greenfield project timeline (Q3 FY27 start) and ramp-up pace; construction risk.
Pending duty decision on cotton imports; CCI procurement share (about 33-34%) influences domestic prices.
Forex mark-to-market swings on open export and import items; Q4 contained a notional charge.
Integration and value addition of acquired downstream businesses; long-term plans to be disclosed after 6-9 months.
Macro risk from multiple wars and higher inflation forecasts, per management.
Group company revenue fell over FY23-FY25; FY26 expected flat, growth of 15-20% in FY27 needs delivery.

539221|2026-06.headline: Sportking Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin reached about 18.8% on yarn spreads of INR133/kg versus INR107 last quarter, with management guiding 18-20% margins to be hard to sustain.
539221|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong start, with healthy revenue growth and a significant profitability improvement driven by better cotton yarn realisations, strong export demand and disciplined raw material buying. The overall spread rose to INR133/kg from INR107 in the prior quarter, and the EBITDA margin was cited at about 18.8%. Management said the margin is elevated, expects the next two quarters to stay around these levels, and expects longer-term margins near 15% after the Odisha plant. The solar project started commercial operations late in the prior quarter (about 10 days of contribution) and is guided to save about INR15 crore a year, with the full 90 days flowing from the current month.

segments.name: Cotton yarn
segments.commentary: Better realisations cited as main driver of margin expansion; spread rose to INR133/kg from INR107/kg. Management said the Odisha plant will add to revenue from Q4.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Management targets a 55:45 export-to-domestic split. China and Bangladesh together account for about 60-70% of Sportking's exports; China's incremental yarn demand was the main driver of the recent uptick.

segments.name: Fabric and garments (proposed acquisitions)
segments.commentary: Proposed acquisitions of Marvel Dyers and Sobhagia Sales are expected to add 8-10% to top line and similar EBITDA share from next year, with about INR250 crore impact from next financial year once the deal completes.

capex_capacity: Greenfield 150,000-spindle expansion in Odisha: first-phase production expected in Q3 FY27, full project targeted within FY27; announced cost about INR975-1,000 crore.
Management expects 30-40% of potential revenue from the new plant in Q4 FY27 and targets 90% plant utilisation by March 2027 and 96-97% by the start of FY28; ramp-up expected to take 5-6 months.
Odisha margins expected at least 300-400 bps above existing plants, per management.
Odisha incentives: INR2.50/unit power subsidy, 30% capital subsidy with no cap, land subsidy tied to employment, and about INR7,000 per employee employment subsidy.
Land is available to triple Odisha capacity; further capex depends on balance sheet and leverage comfort.
Solar project commissioned and operating; expected to cut annual power cost by 12-15%.
demand_pricing: Management said demand from all markets remains healthy and expects festive-season support domestically.

Global cotton yarn demand improved as China became a large buyer, pushing Indian yarn prices higher; management said China imports about 20,000 tonnes against India's roughly 400,000 tonnes monthly output.
Order book kept at 70-90 days, similar to end of last quarter.
Cotton prices rose about 10-11% over the last quarter; management says most purchases were made about 3 months earlier and that Q2 should be similar to or better than Q1.
India-UK FTA signed last month, but no orders yet; management expects 6-9 months for orders to reflect in the order book.

Management expects China to remain a buyer because Chinese cotton prices are above international levels. Bangladesh's spinning sector is under strain from gas and capital costs, which helps Indian yarn demand.
Exports to the US are indirect via downstream vendors whose offtake has roughly doubled in the last 6 months.
guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected around 18-19% for the next two quarters; longer-term margin guided around 15% after Odisha, with 12-14% described as the comfortable range.
FY27 revenue target about INR3,000 crore (around 20% growth); FY28 target above INR4,000 crore with Odisha.
Solar savings about INR15 crore annually; full 90-day contribution expected from the current month.
Absolute EBITDA expected to keep rising in FY28 even if percentage margins moderate.
Cotton import duty waiver runs to 31 October; management is lobbying the government to extend it and says FY27 inventory is already covered for two quarters.
Acquisition completion expected in about one more quarter, with full impact from next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin sustainability and what drove the 18.8% margin, including the import duty effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cotton import duty made no contribution to Q1 because raw material was already bought; margins should stay around current levels for two quarters, with absolute EBITDA expected to keep trending higher.

qa_highlights.question: Is the spread of INR133/kg sustainable for a year or two?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to predict precisely, expects cotton prices to ease after the new crop, and said the inventory effect will be larger in the next two quarters because Q1 realisations lagged cotton prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Odisha plant reach high utilisation and what is the revenue run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 96-97% utilisation by start of FY28; no Q3 revenue assumed, with 30-40% of potential revenue from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the merger financing and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly preferential shares, with cash outflow of about INR25-30 crore and no meaningful incremental debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity beyond Odisha Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Land exists to triple Odisha capacity; further capex depends on the balance sheet and leverage comfort.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term product mix shift toward value-added products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said value-added fabric and garment share would be about 10% in the next year; longer-term plans to be announced once there is more visibility.

risks_watch: Cyclicality: management itself flagged 18-20% margins as likely not sustainable long term and cited FY22 peaks as an aberration.
Cotton input cost: prices up 10-11% in the last quarter; management expects a moderation after October, but the import duty waiver ends on 31 October unless extended.
Capacity additions: spread strength may attract new spindle capacity; management says it has not seen announced projects.
Odisha ramp-up: 5-6 month ramp, targeted 90% utilisation by March 2027, and margin accretion (300-400 bps) depend on execution.
Acquisitions of Marvel Dyers and Sobhagia Sales: completion timing has slipped and the contribution is still under progress.
Export concentration: China and Bangladesh make up 60-70% of exports; the China-driven demand could reverse.

So I won't take it as a benchmark for the volatility of margins. Otherwise, they stay between 12% to 14%, which is where we are comfortable actually.

539254|2026-03.headline: AESL FY26 capitalisation of about INR15,300 crores; FY27 capex guided at INR21,000-22,000 crores and capitalisation at INR21,000-22,000 crores.
539254|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as a year of heavy commissioning, led by the Mumbai HVDC project (INR7,000 crores, commissioned 15 March 2026) and 82.29 lakh smart meters installed in the year against a 70 lakh target. Management guided FY27 capex to about INR21,000-22,000 crores (transmission about INR15,500 crores) and FY28 to about INR22,000-25,000 crores, with capitalisation of INR21,000-22,000 crores in FY27 and about INR13,000 crores in FY28. Credit ratings were described as improved to AAA+/AAA for most assets, with interest costs falling, and net leverage is to be held at 4.5x-4.7x. Management declined to give formal EBITDA guidance but said transmission EBITDA could reach about 3x current levels over 36-40 months and that FY27 consolidated EBITDA could be about INR11,500 crores versus INR8,726 crores in FY26 (as stated by the CEO).

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY26 HVDC and capitalisation translate into FY27-28, and how much CWIP reconciles with the transmission capitalisation guide?

qa_highlights.question: How should the leverage be viewed given negative free cash flow in FY26?

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA contribution from FY26 commissioned transmission projects and the win rate in tenders?

qa_highlights.question: How will Mumbai HVDC revenue be booked in FY27, and what is the status of Pole 2?

qa_highlights.question: Why did smart meter operating EBITDA figures differ between the nine-month and full-year presentations?

qa_highlights.question: Can operating profit double or triple, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said FY27 consolidated EBITDA could be about INR11,500 crores; CFO said transmission EBITDA could reach about 3x current levels in 36-40 months, with distribution EBITDA about INR2,500 crores rising to INR3,000-3,200 crores and smart metering EBITDA INR2,400-3,000 crores once fully built.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin on the 1.5 GW C&I trading book?

539300|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 120.64% YoY to INR276.33 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to 8.18% on raw-material and crude-linked cost pressure.
539300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR276.33 crores, up 120.64% YoY and 39.85% QoQ, with PAT of INR15.04 crores (up 130.67% YoY). EBITDA rose 94.41% YoY to INR22.59 crores, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 9.28% a year earlier and 10.19% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the margin squeeze to dyes, chemicals, boiler fuel, LABSA and PP packaging costs linked to geopolitical crude volatility, which hit the textile business hardest. Installed FMCG and FMCG-intermediate capacity rose to 20,840 tons per month after a 1,700 MT soap line was commissioned at Roorkee. Management guides FY27 revenue of INR900-1,000 crores and a ~6% profitability level, with a further 0.75-1% improvement in FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Dyes, chemicals, consumables, boiler fuel and LABSA rose; PP packaging spiked. Textile prices could not be raised in Q1; management expects normalisation by Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue INR900-1,000 crores, FY28 growth 15-20%; FY27 profitability about 6%, rising 0.75-1% in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation at 50-55%; another 25-30% expected by FY28; little new capex needed for one to one-and-a-half years.

qa_highlights.answer: Roorkee capacity was funded from the subsidiary's retained earnings. INR98.65 crores raised was used for Bhilwara food and Guwahati soap/noodle/cosmetics facilities, not for Sunrakshakk Agro acquisition, which predated the raise. No further fundraising is planned.

qa_highlights.answer: Offset the Q1 cost increase and raise utilisation of recently added capacity over three to four quarters.

539301|2026-03.headline: FY26 bookings hit record INR1,550 crore (+22% YoY) while FY26 revenue fell to INR564 crore from INR713 crore on revenue-recognition timing.
539301|2026-03.overview: Arvind SmartSpaces reported record FY26 bookings of INR1,550 crore, up 22% YoY, with Q4 bookings crossing INR600 crore for the first time. Full-year revenue declined to INR564 crore from INR713 crore, which management attributed to timing of revenue recognition and occupation certificates slipping into FY27, while adjusted EBITDA fell to INR156 crore and PAT to INR103 crore. Q4 PAT rose 103% YoY to INR44 crore on revenue of INR155 crore. Business development added projects worth INR3,140 crore in FY26, and a further INR2,400 crore Mumbai high-rise was signed after year-end.

539301|2026-06.headline: Arvind SmartSpaces Q1 FY27 presales rose 147% YoY to INR432 crores; PAT jumped to INR97 crores on Orchards Phase 1 BU receipt.

Revenue rose to INR318 crores from INR102 crores and adjusted EBITDA to INR150 crores from INR25 crores, mainly from Orchards Phase 1 in Bengaluru receiving BU. qa_highlights.question: How is OCF flattening and what is FY27 OCF guidance?

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and leverage comfort level?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to equity at 0.29x; management comfortable up to 1:1 and expects gradual debt increase, funded by OCF and debt lines.

qa_highlights.question: How will BD of INR600-1,000 crores be funded?

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for an annuity or commercial portfolio?

Launch execution: 6 launches worth INR3,000-3,500 crores this year depend on approvals, including Pen Khopoli.

Guidance inconsistency: BD cash deployment quoted as INR600-900 crores in one answer and INR600-1,000 crores in another.

539302|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR 2,121 crore, while FY26 order inflow of ~INR 7,210 crore missed the INR 10,000 crore target by about 28%.
539302|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 2,121 crore (+13% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 237 crore (+2% YoY, margin 11.17%) and PAT of INR 153 crore (+18%). FY26 revenue was INR 6,107 crore (+16%), EBITDA INR 750 crore (12.3% margin) and PAT INR 412 crore (+18%). Order inflow missed guidance after cancellation of a INR 1,563 crore BESS order by the West Bengal electricity department, and the water division faced certification delays. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, order inflow of about INR 12,000 crore and EBITDA margin of about 12.5%.

segments.name: Power vs non-power mix
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 57% power and 43% non-power; FY26 was 64% power and 36% non-power. Backlog is about 70% power and 30% non-power.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 94% domestic and 6% international; FY26 was 95% domestic and 5% international. International work is mainly O&M and manpower supply (Middle East, Nigeria), with international revenue of INR 327 crore in FY26 versus INR 292 crore in FY25.

segments.name: MDO (mining, KBP and SAIL/Tasra)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 MDO revenue was INR 226 crore, including INR 117 crore in March. Management targets INR 500 crore in FY27 and INR 1,250 crore in FY28, with EBITDA margin of about 15% now rising toward 20% at peak rated capacity (FY29-30).

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M is the highest-margin business at about 15-16% EBITDA. Management cites O&M order growth of about 8% and about 4,100 MW of O&M orders in FY26, including a INR 279 crore Mumbai Monorail/metro O&M contract.

segments.name: EPC / civil
segments.commentary: Construction margins are below 8-10%. The BOP EPC order for the 800 MW Singareni project from BHEL is about INR 2,550 crore. Electrical transmission work has ended and was moved into civil.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, which management says it is confident of achieving.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR 12,000 crore, mainly BOP EPC and O&M; FY28 target INR 12,000-15,000 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12.5% including other income, up 0.25-0.3 percentage points.
MDO revenue targets: about INR 500 crore in FY27 (KBP INR 350 crore, Tasra/SAIL INR 150 crore), INR 1,250 crore in FY28, and about INR 2,100-2,200 crore at full capacity in FY29-30.
Blended EBITDA is guided to rise about 0.5% a year to 14% by FY30 and about 14.25% in FY31.
FY27 capex of about INR 400 crore at Power Mech level (washery) and about INR 400 crore at the Tasra SPV, without debt.
capex_capacity: KBP mine (Kurmitar area) began production in November 2025; the client is lifting above contract capacity, and FY26 offtake was about 1.6 million tonnes.
Tasra washery construction should finish by December 2026, with washed coal from Q4 FY27 and Tasra production from mid Q4 FY27. Management says the Tasra ramp-up reaches peak rated capacity in FY29.
Target full capacity: KBP about 5 million tonnes by FY30; SAIL/Tasra about 4 million tonnes by FY29.
Current metro O&M covers about 1,095 operational km in India, expected to reach 2,000 km; Mumbai light rail O&M covers 15 stations.
Annual power commissioning is expected to reach about 8,000 MW a year, which management sees as driving installation, civil and O&M demand.
demand_pricing: Management identified about INR 70,000 crore of opportunities for FY27 across power, non-power, metro O&M and EPC. Its past bidding is about INR 40,000-50,000 crore at a hit ratio of about 15%.
BOP opportunities worth about INR 15,000 crore are being bid for 2-3 projects, with a target of one more BOP win in FY27.
Pricing is the main constraint on BHEL packages; management says BHEL is changing its packaging approach.
Named opportunities: BALCO O&M about INR 1,500 crore, Butibori O&M about INR 700 crore, and NMDC EPC tenders worth about INR 8,000-10,000 crore with Thyssenkrupp as partner.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value remains, with about INR 128 crore of work awaiting certification and INR 90 crore receivable. Management has stopped new water bids.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 10,000 crore order target missed, and is FY27 better?
qa_highlights.answer: The miss was mainly the INR 1,563 crore West Bengal BESS cancellation. Management expects West Bengal to re-tender, and says Bangalore Metro and Monorail (L1 in April) support about INR 10,000 crore; FY27 target is INR 12,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook given water division delays and labour code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 EBITDA of about 12.5%, up 0.25-0.3 points, helped by more O&M and EPC mix. The Labour Code gratuity provision in Q4 was about INR 4.5 crore for the full-year impact.

qa_highlights.question: Do escalation clauses protect margins against commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic contracts carry PVC/escalation clauses that are billed to clients. International business is mainly O&M manpower, so impact is limited; the 1.2-1.5% of international order book is largely O&M.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDO FY28 cut from INR 1,800-1,900 crore to INR 1,250 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The KBP washery is not ready on the CCL side, so offtake is conservatively put at INR 350 crore in FY27. The SAIL/Tasra ramp from zero to 4 million tonnes in one year is treated as a challenge, so FY28 is INR 750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDO margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin is about 15% at present, and management expects about 1 percentage point a year, reaching 20%-21% at peak rated capacity around FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Are there labour shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount is above 40,000, with 70-75% in labour roles and about 18,000 in O&M. Management says construction and installation labour is the constraint, but schedules have been met so far.

risks_watch: Order inflow execution: FY26 missed by about 28%, and the FY27 target of INR 12,000 crore depends on BOP wins against BHEL's changed packaging approach and pricing.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value is stalled pending central and state fund release, and certification delays weigh on margins.
MDO ramp-up: KBP and Tasra volumes depend on client offtake, the CCL washery, and the rainy season. The FY27 MDO target (INR 500 crore) is well above the Q4 monthly run-rate once March is excluded.
Commodity and labour inflation: steel, cement and diesel prices have risen. Recovery relies on PVC clauses, and labour availability is a constraint.
Management's 1-point-a-year margin expansion in MDO and blended EBITDA targets rest on O&M and EPC mix shifts.
539302|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and bullish on long-term power and O&M demand, but cautious on near-term order inflow and the water division. Management was explicit about the BESS cancellation and the MDO timing shortfall, and gave specific numbers on most questions. Some answers on segment figures and MDO revenue were revised during the call, which weakens the precision of the guidance.
key_quotes: Otherwise, our numbers would have been much better in order backlog.
Of course, on the BOP side, we are going to bid for two- three projects, that's worth INR 15000 crores.
We are confident of achieving that, and even the MDO business ramp -up of production is happening, and we are more focused on the high -margin O&M business.

rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12.5% incl. other income, up 0.25-0.3 pts from 12.3% in FY26, helped by O&M and EPC mix, with MDO margin (about 15%) expected to rise about 1 pt a year toward 20-21% at peak capacity.

rows.why: KBP mine already producing since Nov 2025 (FY26 offtake ~1.6 Mt vs target ~5 Mt by FY30) and Tasra washery (INR 400 cr capex) is under construction, with ~4 Mt targeted by FY29; ramp is conditional on client offtake and CCL washery readiness.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 21% on FY26 revenue of INR 6,107 cr, with MDO revenue targeted at INR 500 cr in FY27 vs INR 226 cr in Q4 FY26 alone (of which INR 117 cr in March), though the FY27 MDO target looks stretched.

rows.why: Only committed capex is INR 400 cr at Power Mech (washery) plus INR 400 cr at Tasra SPV, both debt-free; no utilisation figure is given, and no new plant or line has been announced, so a fresh capex round is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 order inflow missed the INR 10,000 cr target by about 28% (INR 7,210 cr), and FY27 order target of INR 12,000 cr depends on one more BOP win and re-tender of the cancelled INR 1,563 cr West Bengal BESS order.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: MDO FY28 target was already cut from INR 1,800-1,900 cr to INR 1,250 cr, FY27 MDO target of INR 500 cr is well above the Q4 run-rate ex-March, water division has ~INR 900 cr stalled with INR 128 cr awaiting certification, and FY26 orders missed by ~28%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed; the only new business lines are MDO ramp-ups already in motion.

rows.label: FY27 order inflow target INR 12,000 cr
rows.why: FY26 inflow was ~INR 7,210 cr (72% of target); FY27 needs BOP wins (~INR 15,000 cr BOP opportunities in 2-3 bids, target one more win), plus Bangalore Metro/Monorail (~INR 10,000 cr, L1 in April) and possible West Bengal re-tender.

rows.label: Water division stall
rows.why: About INR 900 cr contract value stalled pending central/state fund release, INR 128 cr awaiting certification and INR 90 cr receivable; management has stopped new water bids, so this drag persists.

rows.label: BHEL package pricing
rows.why: Pricing is the main constraint on BHEL packages and BHEL is changing its packaging approach; the 800 MW Singareni BOP (~INR 2,550 cr) and NMDC EPC (INR 8,000-10,000 cr with Thyssenkrupp) hinge on this.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 21% revenue growth, 12.5% margin and long-term power/O&M demand, but cautious on order inflow, water division and MDO timing; analysts pressed on the order miss, MDO FY28 cut and margin path, and some segment figures were revised during the call.

539334|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 21.1% to Rs 976.6 crore, but Unit 5/6 commissioning is stalled by raw-material price spikes, with FY27 revenue guided to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore.
539334|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 976.6 crore (+21.1%), EBITDA Rs 99.5 crore (10.2% margin) and PAT Rs 70.1 crore (7.1% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was about Rs 218 crore with EBITDA Rs 22.1 crore and PAT Rs 12.9 crore, held back by raw-material availability. Management said it deliberately stopped dispatches in the second week of March 2026 as ammonia and sulphur prices roughly tripled, and new Unit 5 and Unit 6 capacity has not been commissioned. Management lowered its FY27 revenue visibility to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 72,423 MT (+27.9%) for Rs 531.8 crore, with segment revenue up 25.2%. Q4 FY26 sales 13,725 MT (+36% YoY) for Rs 126.4 crore. Management cited H Acid at about Rs 750/kg (from Rs 525-530/kg) and Vinyl Sulphone at about Rs 350/kg (from Rs 240/kg).

segments.name: Fertilisers
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 252,777 MT for Rs 444.8 crore, with segment revenue up 16.5%. Q4 FY26 sales 50,500 MT for Rs 91.8 crore. Management said NBS subsidy was raised on 1 Feb and 1 Apr 2026 but is still not sufficient for current raw-material costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue visibility lowered to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore, assuming about Rs 1,000 crore from existing plants at 65-70% utilisation and Rs 250 crore from Rabi season; no benefit from higher current prices assumed.
Kharif FY27 season expected to contribute no revenue from Unit 5 or Unit 6; start of trial production under evaluation, with management saying it could start within about one month.
Q1 FY27 expected to benefit from liquidating inventory held back in Q4; management said PAT should be about 8-8.5% of revenue and Q1 sales above Rs 250 crore, without firm numbers.
Normal tax rate guided at 22-25% for FY27, with deferred tax expected to rise significantly as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar capitalise.
Management sees 8-10% margins as achievable, while noting that sulphur may settle at about Rs 70-75/kg rather than the earlier Rs 30-35/kg.
capex_capacity: Total planned capex Rs 512 crore; Rs 189 crore incurred as of 31 March 2026, funded by internal accruals and preferential allotment.

Unit 5 (dyes) and Unit 6 are mechanically ready; Unit 6 about 90-95% complete. Commissioning delayed by electricity issues (resolved in March 2026) and raw-material price spikes; no capitalisation yet.
Solar: 1.1 MW DC commissioned at Hisar, Haryana, taking installed capacity to 10.6 MW DC; 10 MW Nanded plant on track, which would take total to 20.6 MW DC.

Planned Rs 350 crore additional facility at Madhya Bharat Phosphates, Meghnagar (Unit 3). About Rs 140 crore sits in AAA-rated bonds, plus Rs 30 crore preferential allotment to promoter; remaining about Rs 180 crore to come from accruals, with possibly 25-30% term loan.
Plant utilisation currently 65-70% per CFO; Unit 1 sulphuric plant was shut for maintenance in Q4.
demand_pricing: Ammonia rose from Rs 40-42/kg to Rs 100+/kg and sulphur from Rs 30/kg to about Rs 100/kg, according to management.
Sulphur rose a further 20% in May 2026 up to 19 May, per management.
Management said demand is weakening as prices rise and that the market is accepting the higher prices for chemicals, though fertiliser acceptability at current prices is uncertain.

Company stopped SSP dispatches in the second week of March 2026 deliberately to avoid selling at the old cost base; management said FY26 revenue would have crossed Rs 1,000 crore if sales had continued for 15 more days.
Management said the company has not factored in the higher current selling prices in its FY27 outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 320-odd crore capex be funded, and what is the maths?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 174 crore and Rs 155 crore phases were funded internally except a Rs 25 crore HDFC solar term loan, and the new Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat project will use about Rs 170 crore of existing bonds and preferential allotment, with the balance from accruals or a possible 25-30% term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-28 outlook for Unit 5 and 6 after the delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the electricity issue was resolved in March 2026 but raw-material price spikes delayed start-up; FY27 revenue is now visualised at Rs 1,250-1,300 crore, with no Kharif contribution from Units 5 and 6.

qa_highlights.question: Will the inventory benefit flow into Q1 FY27, and can it be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 should be better than recent quarters as held-back Q4 inventory is liquidated, but declined to quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue flat YoY in Q4 despite chemical volumes up over 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not answer on the call and said the company would respond through its IR advisor.

qa_highlights.question: What tax rate should be assumed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a normal rate of 22-25% should be used, with deferred tax rising next year as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar are capitalised; the Q4 deferred tax charge of about Rs 4-4.5 crore related to land recognised as right-of-use assets for the Madhya Bharat project.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 PAT fall short of the 8% margin management had earlier signalled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT would have been Rs 75-80 crore without the deferred tax charge and leasehold-land provisions, which brought it to Rs 70 crore for FY26 (about 7%).

risks_watch: Raw-material cost and supply: ammonia and sulphur prices have roughly tripled and remain volatile; management could not predict when they will ease.
Unit 5 and 6 start-up timing is unresolved; the Kharif season is lost and Rabi FY27 is the next opportunity.
Demand and fertiliser affordability at current prices; management said subsidy support is not yet adequate and noted a 10% government cap.
Q1 FY27 inventory-liquidation benefit is unquantified, and management declined to give numbers; also the Q4 revenue-versus-volume gap is unexplained on the call.
Deferred tax and effective tax rate will rise in FY27 as projects capitalise; a term loan may be used for the Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat capex.
Governance and disclosure: management relied on the CFO for most figures and its tone on the call was unusually unstructured.
539334|2026-03.management_tone: Management was candid but cautious, emphasising conservatism and a wait-and-see stance on Units 5 and 6 and on FY27 pricing. Its visibility was often hedged ("I can't read too far"), and it repeatedly deferred detailed numbers to the CFO or to later IR follow-up.
key_quotes: So, sir, let the market be matured. Let the market be accepting these new prices, which are almost three times of the raw material prices of our earlier.
Old numbers will never be seen again.
So we will definitely do Rs. 250 crores in that. Rs. 1000 crores and Rs. 250 crores.

rows.why: Management sees 8-10% margins as achievable and guides Q1 FY27 PAT at 8-8.5% of revenue versus Q4 FY26 PAT margin of 5.8% and FY26 at 7.1%, but sulphur may settle at Rs 70-75/kg versus Rs 30-35/kg earlier and ammonia has risen from Rs 40-42/kg to Rs 100+/kg, so the gain depends on pass-through.

rows.why: FY26 chemical volumes rose 27.9% to 72,423 MT and fertiliser sales were 252,777 MT, but FY27 revenue visibility was cut to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from Rs 1,500 crore, with existing plants at 65-70% utilisation and Rs 250 crore assumed from Rabi season.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 65-70%, so there is no capacity-driven case for new capex, but the Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat (Unit 3) plan is already on the table and management said it is still looking for a better opportunity and right time to start it, so timing is undated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was cut to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from Rs 1,500 crore and management has not factored in higher current selling prices, so an upgrade would need a clear recovery in dispatches that the call does not show.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue has already been cut once (Rs 1,500 crore to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore), demand is weakening as prices rise, Q4 revenue was flat YoY on chemical volume up 36%, and Unit 5/6 timing is unresolved.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: after Unit 5/6 commissioning, Rabi FY27 onward
rows.why: Unit 5 (dyes) and Unit 6 chemical plants are mechanically ready but no product launch timing or product names were given on the call.

rows.label: Q1 FY27 inventory liquidation
rows.why: Management said held-back Q4 inventory will be liquidated in Q1 FY27 and guided Q1 sales above Rs 250 crore versus Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 218.2 crore, though it declined to quantify the benefit.

rows.label: NBS subsidy adequacy for fertilisers
rows.why: NBS subsidy was raised on 1 Feb and 1 Apr 2026 but management says it is still insufficient for current raw-material costs, and a 10% government cap is in place.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q1 FY27 PAT margin of 8-8.5% and on Unit 6 being 90-95% complete, but cautious on Units 5/6 start-up, FY27 pricing and the Rs 350 crore Unit 3 project, deferring numbers to the CFO and IR; analysts probed the unexplained Q4 revenue-versus-volume gap and capex funding.

539334|2026-06.headline: Shree Pushkar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 280-281 crore and EBITDA rose 9.7% to Rs 31.9 crore, despite volumes falling sharply.
539334|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 10% YoY on higher realisations even though fertiliser volumes fell to 66,527 MT from 76,288 MT and chemical volumes fell to 9,113 MT from 14,837 MT. EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2%, with PAT up about 9% to Rs 22.9 crore. Management said acid plants were run at low load due to high sulphur prices and working-capital strain, and Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 are close to trial operation. Management reiterated an FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, which it said could reach Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, with PAT of around 8.5-9%.

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 142 crore, up 4% YoY, on 66,527 MT volume (down from 76,288 MT). Management said inventory is being held in anticipation of higher prices.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 138 crore, up 17.1% YoY, on 9,113 MT (down from 14,837 MT). Acid plants were put on low load; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, with management saying it could reach Rs 1,300-1,400 crore (Rs 1,350-1,400 crore in one answer), and PAT of around 8.5-9%.
Management expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and better than Q2 FY26 (about 110% higher, per management's reply to an analyst's Rs 250-285 crore comparison).
Unit 6 expected to start trials by end-August or September 2026, giving about 4-5 months of operation in FY27.
Next year (FY28) with a full 12 months of Unit 6 could reach Rs 1,700-1,750 crore, per management's personal view.
Management says peak revenue for all units could reach about Rs 1,700 crore at current prices once Unit 6 is on stream.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of Rs 209 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026 against a total planned Rs 512 crore; about Rs 20 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Expansions at Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 and Meghnagar are expected to add 450,000 MT per annum of fertiliser capacity and 72,000 MT per annum of chemical capacity.

Unit 5 dyes plant (small vertical, about Rs 37 crore) and 10 MW DC solar project at Nanded are complete or nearing completion; total solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC once commissioned. Capitalisation not yet announced.
Acquired about 30,000 sq m of land adjacent to Unit 1 at Lote Parshuram for Rs 9.3 crore in Q1.
Madhya Bharat (Madhya Pradesh) project has Rs 60 crore invested to June; timeline 2028. Plant is about twice Unit 6 capacity and includes an 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK integration.
Rs 125 crore in non-lien deposits as of 30 June 2026; capex funded from internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are absorbing higher raw material prices, and demand is recovering after a pause during the West Asia conflict.
Sulphur prices have risen to about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 earlier, per management; ammonia and sulphur shortages followed Hormuz closure.

539336|2026-03.headline: Gujarat Energy FY26 EBITDA rose to INR3,772 crore (from INR3,241 crore) while PAT was flat at INR2,299 crore; the merger became effective 1 May 2026.
539336|2026-03.overview: The GSPC/GSPL merger into Gujarat Gas became effective 1 May 2026, with the company renamed Gujarat Energy from 14 May 2026. Q4 FY26 EBITDA was INR943 crore (vs INR790 crore a year earlier), and CNG volume hit a record 3.6 mmscmd. Morbi ceramic demand ramped sharply to about 8 mmscmd after the Middle East conflict constrained propane and LPG supply. Management said FY26 financials are not like-for-like with FY25 because of the demerger and merger accounting, and gave segment EBITDA for the first time on a call. The board recommended a dividend of INR8.90 per share (about INR835 crore outgo).

segments.commentary: Q4 CNG volume was a record 3.6 mmscmd (up 12% YoY) across 839 stations, with 17.68 lakh vehicles. Domestic PNG customers crossed 24.18 lakh; Q4 PNG industrial volume was 4.19 mmscmd, up about 7% QoQ. Morbi volume rose 21% QoQ to an average of 2.02 mmscmd in Q4.

The company is reviewing options for the 700 MW combined-cycle plant, whose PPA runs to 2036.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in gas trading and the segment profit baseline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recurring trading run rate is about INR1,000-1,100 crore a year. FY26 included about INR200 crore of one-off liability linked to a Petronet LNG back-to-back arrangement, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

GUVNL pays fixed costs of about INR2.5-3 per unit. Management said the plants are not a drag at present, and a steady-state profit cannot be given until a new arrangement is identified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage LNG price risk as Morbi volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brent-linked long-term volumes from Qatar and Uniper are priced competitively against propane. It is also seeking Henry Hub-linked long-term volumes to give stable pricing for Morbi customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the deployment plan for surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has appointed McKinsey to develop a growth and deployment strategy. It expects to share the way forward in the next quarter or a subsequent one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company transfer trading profits to CGD on a cost basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intersegment pricing will be optimised over time as the two segments are evaluated separately. The company now has flexibility to make intersegment sales without the arm's-length constraint.

539336|2026-06.headline: Gujarat Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% to INR9,670 crores and PAT 78% to INR998 crores, led by gas trading EBT of INR726 crores.
539336|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR9,670 crores (up 63% YoY), EBITDA INR1,482 crores (up 65%) and PAT INR998 crores (up 78%), with total sales volume of 15.66 mmscmd. Gas trading EBT rose 206% to INR726 crores, helped by Brent-linked long-term contracts and a Morbi industrial volume surge during the Middle East-driven propane shortage. Management kept FY27 gas trading profit guidance at about INR1,100 crores (reiterated as INR1,100-1,200 crores in one answer) and CGD EBITDA guidance at INR5.5-6.5/scm, while saying Morbi volumes will likely settle near 3 mmscmd as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources.

segments.commentary: Sales volume 12.22 mmscmd, of which 8.9 mmscmd was transferred to CGD and about 3.3 mmscmd was external; EBT INR726 crores. Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd earlier, due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and lower power volumes; long-term third-party volume expected at 4.5-5 mmscmd in FY28-29.

segments.name: CGD - CNG
segments.commentary: Volume 3.76 mmscmd, up 13% from 3.33 mmscmd (Gujarat +12%, outside Gujarat +19%). Network at 844 stations after adding 6 and upgrading 9 in the quarter; plans for more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades in FY27.

segments.name: CGD - PNG domestic
segments.commentary: Added about 59,000 domestic PNG customers in the quarter, taking the base above 2.477 million households. Commercial PNG volume was 0.17 mmscmd with more than 16,600 commercial customers.

segments.name: PNG industrial
segments.commentary: Volume 7.17 mmscmd vs 4.71 mmscmd, up 64%. Morbi averaged 5.67 mmscmd and non-Morbi 2.04 mmscmd; non-Morbi realisation about INR70/scm and Morbi about INR78/scm, against propane at about INR65/scm.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Gas-based plants run at very low utilisation: about 6% PLF at the 51 MW GSEG plant and about 1% at Pipavav in Q1, with peak summer demand the only driver.

segments.name: E&P and renewables
segments.commentary: Q1 FY26 EBITDA was INR7 crores (E&P) and INR14 crores (renewables); Q4 FY26 was INR14 crores and INR5 crores. No Q1 FY27 figures were given on the call.

guidance_outlook: Gas trading profit guidance kept at about INR1,100 crores for FY27 on total trading volume, with a 4-5% margin target; one answer cited INR1,100-1,200 crores.
CGD EBITDA guidance kept at INR5.5-6.5/scm; Q2 FY27 is the earliest point for firmer FY27 numbers given Middle East volatility.
CGD capex guided at about INR1,000 crores; no capex planned for gas trading; propane import terminal capex excluded and at early study stage, with capex over the next two years.
Morbi gas volume expected at about 3 mmscmd near term; 1.8-2 mmscmd assumed as a floor on one-month contracts.
Non-Morbi industrial volume targeted at 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise.
Long-term sourcing about 28% (about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent) today, targeted at least 4 million tonnes by 2030; new long-term supply from 2028.
Concrete plan for deploying about INR7,200 crores cash expected by Q3 FY27.
GSPL Transmission listing expected towards early September 2026; Q2 results around mid-November.
capex_capacity: CGD capex of about INR1,000 crores guided for FY27; INR127 crores invested in CGD infrastructure in Q1.
CNG network at 844 stations; more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades planned in FY27.
Pipeline network about 45,900 km across six states and one union territory.
Own propane import and storage terminal near Morbi: sites shortlisted in Gujarat, detailed project report pending, capex over about two years and not in the INR1,000 crore plan.

demand_pricing: Morbi current run-rate about 3 mmscmd of gas vs about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from the US and Venezuela after July.

qa_highlights.question: How do 15.66 mmscmd total volume, 12.2 mmscmd gas trading and 12.34 mmscmd CGD reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15.66 is the company total and CGD is 12.34; after removing the 8.9 mmscmd intercompany sale to CGD, external sales are about 3.32 mmscmd.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current Morbi run-rate and how does pricing compare with propane?

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNG growth outlook for the rest of FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Will third-party gas trading volumes recover, and what is the long-term range?

qa_highlights.question: Is there a sourcing breakup for CGD and gas trading, and what is the long-term share?

qa_highlights.question: What is the CGD EBITDA position against guidance, and why is it below range?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD EBITDA was about INR5.18/scm, below the INR5.5-6.5/scm guidance, which management attributed to a larger volume base. Management kept the guidance and said it looks at portfolio margins rather than segment-level Morbi margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-Morbi industrial volume plans and constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Morbi volume is about 2-2.2 mmscmd; management targets at least 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise. It cited infrastructure build-out, with about 86 new industries added in April-June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Morbi volume floor and how is the propane terminal funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumed 1.8-2 mmscmd as a floor on one-month contracts. The propane import terminal is at the site-shortlisting stage, excluded from the INR1,000 crore CGD capex, and would take about two years to build after a detailed project report.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR7,200 crore cash and dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is about INR7,200 crores, with a concrete deployment plan by Q3 FY27 covering CNG, pipelines and energy diversification. It cited dividends of about INR835 crores under Government of Gujarat guidelines.

539359|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 36.2% YoY to INR138.46 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.02% on raw material and gas cost spikes.
539359|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue for FY26 reached INR482.95 crore, up 35.32% YoY, with EBITDA of INR71.03 crore (14.71% margin) and PAT of INR23.20 crore. Q4 EBITDA margin dropped to 12.02% from the 16-17% range management cited earlier, which management attributed to raw material, gas, freight and outsourced labour cost increases in March 2026. Management expects margins to recover toward 15-16% if the war-related cost disruption does not worsen, and guided Q1 FY27 revenue at a similar run rate to Q4. Capacity is about 72,000 MTPA with FY26 output of 52,620 MT, and the company plans about 7,800 MT of foundry addition in H1 FY27.

segments.commentary: Contributes about 10-15% of revenue and about 20% of the order book; management targets 30% in three years. Margin is about 1-2% higher than conventional castings.

segments.commentary: Not yet material; product development and qualification ongoing with three to four products developed. Initial contributions expected in FY27.

Greenfield LFC economics: 3,000 MT capacity at about INR75 crore versus INR120-150 crore for conventional, roughly 50% lower capex.
Hoshiarpur land acquired via ARC auction was withdrawn after litigation; refund received. Company is looking for fresh land in about two to three months for capacity beyond 1-2 years.
demand_pricing: Customers expect 6-8% growth in FY27 with H2 facing a high base; company expects about 15% from new products and projects.
Company says it gained share with almost all customers: market grew 16-17% while the company grew 34%.
Top three customers (M&M, Swaraj, TAFE, Escorts named) contribute about 50-55% of revenue.
Order book described as overbooked; Vishal's estimate of INR500-600 crore was affirmed as easily achievable, but no official figure was stated.

Raw material cost up about 4-6% in March; management says raw material is passed through with about a one-quarter lag, while freight pass-through is being negotiated (monthly for some customers, quarterly for others).

Exports started to South Korea (one lot shipped, another going); Europe being explored. US subsidiary (Omnia Engineering Inc., Delaware) acquired for $50,000 with up to $100,000 planned; not yet operational.

qa_highlights.question: What is installed capacity and maximum utilisation, and why have EBITDA margins fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Installed capacity is 72,000 MT; utilisation about 73-74%, with 80-85% achievable this year. Margin fell to 12% because raw material prices rose sharply in March, aggravated by gas issues; recovery expected from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall in Q4, and will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material rose about 4-6%, and gas, outsourced labour, manpower and freight costs also rose in March. Management expects a reversion to 15-16% margins if war-related disruption does not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan and funding for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR25-30 crore, with about INR35 crore for the 7,800 MT project per management. FY28 LFC project of 2,400 MT needs about INR60-70 crore, funded by debt and equity; FY27 funded by debt only.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels and leverage comfort?

qa_highlights.question: What is the US entity's margin profile and plan?

539400|2026-03.headline: Mallcom Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 7% YoY to INR147 crore, but EBITDA margin fell 185 bps to 9.34% on raw material costs.
539400|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was INR147 crore (+7% YoY), with EBITDA down 11% YoY to INR14 crore and margin at 9.34%, and PAT of INR6 crore (4.29% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR540 crore (+11%), EBITDA INR61 crore (11.21% margin, down 130 bps), and PAT INR30 crore; FY25 PAT included a one-time INR25 crore land-sale gain, so the years are not directly comparable. Export OEM realisations fell on weak US and EU demand and tariff-driven concessions, while the domestic business grew about 20%. Both new units (Sanand, Gujarat and Chandipur, West Bengal) are now commissioned and ramping up.

segments.commentary: Realisations fell on weak US and EU demand and concessions to hold share. South America, Australia, Russia and Africa were described as doing well; Europe and US weak; Middle East okay. LatAm sales are white label.

segments.commentary: In-house manufacturing started as import substitutes; management says pricing is competitive with imports and margins are similar to company level. India PU glove imports estimated at INR80-90 crore.

segments.commentary: Commercial production started; running at about 50% utilisation, with INR40 crore minimum annual revenue targeted from existing capacity.

US: volumes fell, but management says this reflects tariff conditions, not product, quality or price. India is outside the US TAA list, so an FTA is seen as key to regaining share; order cycles run 3 months to 2-2.5 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-12% growth is the bare minimum and it is confident of it. It wants to return to pre-investment EBITDA margins, which it describes as the profile it would like to maintain.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO: no term loan; working capital debt is about flat YoY at INR110-115 crore. Expects further reduction and most debt repaid over about 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key domestic demand drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour code formalisation, BIS standards tightening, rising worker awareness, wider distribution, more marketing and fleet, and import substitution. Management says domestic growth is sustainable.

qa_highlights.answer: India imports an estimated INR80-90 crore of PU gloves; PVC gumboot market size was not quantified. Export revenue is also targeted for both products.

539400|2026-06.headline: Mallcom Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 25% QoQ to Rs 110 crore, while EBITDA margin rose 317 bps to 12.51% on pricing and raw material relief.
539400|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating revenue was Rs 110 crore, down 25% QoQ, driven by weaker international sales and West Asia disruption. EBITDA held flat QoQ at Rs 14 crore, with margin up to 12.51%, and PAT rose 5% QoQ to Rs 7 crore (6.03% margin). Domestic revenue of Rs 64 crore grew 10% QoQ and was the highest-ever Q1 domestic number; international revenue was Rs 46 crore. Management said port congestion and weak Western demand cost the company a targeted double-digit export growth.

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 64 crore, up 10% QoQ and the highest Q1 domestic revenue to date; brand recall and the SMILE reseller programme (over 1,000 resellers) cited as drivers.

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 46 crore, down sharply QoQ on weak Western demand and port congestion; management says exports are about 55% of the mix. Europe is down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1 against about Rs 170 crore for last year.

segments.commentary: Three lines now operating (helmets, foam caps, nasal caps); FY26 revenue about Rs 5 crore (Q4 only); FY27 minimum target Rs 40 crore, described as on track.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both weak Western demand and port congestion. The company had targeted at least double-digit export growth, which it missed this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise its Rs 1,000 crore target for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not revise the target now, calling it a stretch, and levers include capacity, distribution, new geographies, FTAs and larger contracts.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO: minimum FY27 target of Rs 40 crore, on track after Q1. FY26 was about Rs 5 crore. Three lines are operating; more capacity is being considered.

rows.label: Large US or LATAM export contracts

539404|2026-03.headline: Satin Creditcare FY26 consolidated PAT rose 79% to INR330 crores; Q4 PAT up 125% QoQ, with FY27 standalone AUM growth guided at 15-20%.
539404|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated AUM of INR15,174 crores (up 19% YoY), revenue of INR3,161 crores (up 23%) and PPOP of INR928 crores (up 23%). Consolidated PAT was INR330 crores for FY26, and Q4 PAT rose 640% YoY and 125% QoQ, which management attributed to lower credit costs and growth, not one-offs. Standalone GNPA was 3.1% at March 2026 and credit cost fell to 3.8% for FY26 from 4.6% in FY25, with Q4 at 2.5% standalone and 2.2% consolidated. Management guided FY27 standalone AUM growth of 15-20% and credit cost of 3-3.5%, and raised its 2030 consolidated AUM target to INR32,000 crores from INR25,000 crores.

financial_highlights.change: NIM 13.23% in FY26 vs 12.42% in FY25

financial_highlights.value: FY26 3.8% standalone; 3.55% consolidated; Q4 2.5% standalone, 2.2% consolidated (INR79 crores)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 standalone -77 bps vs 4.6% in FY25

segments.name: Standalone microfinance (JLG)
segments.commentary: Standalone AUM INR12,853 crores (+14% YoY) with disbursements of INR11,202 crores; UP is 23% of portfolio with PAR 90 of 3%, Assam PAR 90 0.7%, Punjab 1.5%. Stage 3 coverage 73% (from 67% in Dec 2025); on-book provisions INR273 crores (2.9%) vs RBI requirement INR172 crores.

segments.name: Satin Housing Finance (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,267 crores, 3-year CAGR 36%; GNPA about 3%, CRAR 53.8%; ICRA A- stable. Average yield about 15.5-16%.

segments.name: Satin Finserv (SFL, MSME subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,054 crores, up 92.5% YoY, 3-year CAGR 66%; 121 branches in 14 states; disbursed INR255 crores across 34 green loans. Lending is secured by receivables, equipment and property, per management.

segments.name: Satin Technologies (STL)
segments.commentary: Enterprise tech (HRMS, LMS, core banking, cybersecurity, agentic AI); first two clients within two months of incorporation; strategic stake in QTrino (post-quantum cryptography) acquired January 2026.

segments.name: Satin Growth Alternatives (SGAL)
segments.commentary: SEBI licence received for INR200 crore Category II AIF, a gender-lens impact fund for rural MSMEs; MOU with SBI for co-investment; progressing toward first close with soft commitments.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone AUM growth 15-20% YoY, implying about INR14,800-15,100 crores.
FY27 standalone credit cost target 3-3.5% vs 3.8% in FY26.
Consolidated AUM growth management estimate about 25-30% (average), so consolidated AUM roughly doubles toward the 2030 target.
2030 consolidated AUM target raised to INR32,000 crores from INR25,000 crores; non-MFI share target 30% (17% today).

NIM expected stable at about 12-13% consolidated (management also cited 13.5-14% over a longer period); no explicit ROA guidance, but management said ROA should improve on FY26's 2.6%, and that a >3% ROA is 'positive' rather than guided.
Cost of funds expected stable to lower; management says it could fall further as repo rates decline.
risks_watch: Q4 overall collection efficiency of just over 97% versus 99.9% X-bucket; monitor whether April holds and whether geopolitics or inflation (fuel prices) affects collections and demand.
Consolidated PAT is sensitive to forex and treasury gains: INR144 crores consolidated derecognition gain, of which INR92 crores is FX-related; management says this reverses over time.
Q4 PAT surge partly reflects lower credit cost; sustainability depends on the 3-3.5% FY27 credit cost target being met.
Yield regulation: incremental MFI yield about 25% and RBI commentary on interest rates; management says the pricing is justified but did not comment on future caps.
Subsidiary ramp-up (SGAL first close, STL client wins) is still early; the consolidated 25-30% growth and 30% non-MFI mix by 2030 depend on it.
Standalone net worth (INR3,129 crores) exceeds consolidated (INR2,868 crores) due to an old revaluation gain, which has limited analytical value.
539404|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on asset quality, profitability and diversification, with strong claims on Q4 performance. Management was evasive on specifics: declined to give ROA guidance, the April collection-efficiency number and the Q4 absolute consolidated PAT, and gave a vague answer on the RBI yield question.
key_quotes: Consolidated PAT grew 640% year -on-year and 125% quarter -on-quarter.
There's no one-off.
We are not growing blindly. We are growing into our infrastructure with the discipline that has defined Satin.
So there is no question where I think it could be singled out as in terms of tax and it's an interest rate play which is going to be there.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about Satin Finserv's customer profile, collateral and underwriting approach.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SFL serves graduated MFI customers and green-finance/micro-enterprise borrowers, underwrites on cash flows and internal scores with data analytics, and lends on secured terms (receivables, equipment, property). It did not give a percentage of the book secured by property; LTV is about 40-45%.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for April X-bucket collection efficiency and whether geopolitical issues are causing stress.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April is holding at a similar level to Q4 (99.9%) but did not give a figure, and said there is no stress from the geopolitical situation in any state. Q4 overall collection efficiency was a little over 97%.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether there was any one-off in Q4 PAT, including forex.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no one-off; Aditi Singh attributed the Q4 PAT rise to reduced credit cost and the growth strategy. Management did not separately quantify the Q4 absolute consolidated PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for FY27 ROA guidance and whether ROA above 3% is achievable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give explicit ROA guidance, saying it is a function of AUM growth and credit cost; it said it expects ROA to be better than FY26's 2.6% and that the direction is positive.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the consolidated AUM path to the 2030 target and the growth pace.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 15-20% guidance applies to standalone MFI only; consolidated growth is expected to average about 25-30%, which supports the revised INR32,000 crore 2030 AUM target (from INR25,000 crores).

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the INR144 crore net gain on derecognition of financial instruments and whether treasury income is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consolidated INR144 crore line includes a INR92 crore FX effect offset by a corresponding finance-cost item, while derecognition gains are DA income and fair-value gains are treasury income on mutual funds and forex contracts. Management said treasury income is incidental to liquidity, and that NIM is broadly stable at 13.5-14% over a longer period.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the RBI yield-cap risk and whether the MFI yield of about 25% is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the regulator's interest-rate focus should be read in the context of financial inclusion, doorstep delivery, elevated credit cost and cost of funds, and risk-based pricing. It did not say how it sees future caps and said there is no question of a one-off yield cut.
